items.title: Assainissement de Conakry : Vivo Energy Guinée fait un don en carburant à travers la Chambre des Mines de Guinée
items.description: Dans le cadre de ses engagements en matière de responsabilité sociétale, Vivo Energy Guinée apporte son soutien aux efforts d'assainissement de la capitale à travers un don de carburant, destiné à l'Agence Nationale de l'Assainissement et de la Salubrité Publique (ANASP). Cette contribution s'inscrit dans une initiative de solidarité coordonnée par la Chambre des Mines de Guinée (CMG), en réponse à la situation d'urgence consécutive au drame de Dar-es-Salam et à l’appel à la mobilisation de Monsieur le Premier Ministre. Conakry, le 7 octobre 2026 – Vivo Energy Guinée, entreprise spécialisée dans la distribution et la commercialisation des carburants et lubrifiants de marque Shell en Guinée sous licence, œuvre pour soutenir les communautés locales. Sa contribution à travers la remise officielle d’un don de carburant vise à renforcer les moyens logistiques nécessaires au transport des déchets de Conakry vers le nouveau site de Kouria, faciliter le désengorgement des zones de transit et de transfert et soutenir la continuité des opérations d'assainissement. La cérémonie de remise s'est tenue au siège de Vivo Energy Guinée, où le Directeur Général, M. Massamba Toure, accompagné des membres de son Comité de Direction, a accueilli Mme Fatoumata Binta Diallo, Cheffe de Cabinet de la Primature, et M. Thierno Souleymane Bah, Conseiller chargé de la Coordination interministérielle et du Suivi des réformes, représentant le Premier ministre. L’équipe de la chambre des Mines représenté par M. le Directeur Exécutif M. François Phopho Kamano a marqué son implication par sa présence, qui a permis de procéder par la voie privilégiée, à la remise du don de carburant effectuée lors de cette rencontre, à l’endroit du Directeur Général de l'ANASP M. Mamoudou Diané. Un engagement sociétal au service des communautés Prenant la parole à cette occasion, le Directeur Général de Vivo Energy Guinée, M. Massamba Toure, a souligné que cette contribution traduit la volonté de l'entreprise d'apporter une réponse concrète aux défis auxquels font face les communautés. « Pour Vivo Energy, la responsabilité sociétale fait partie de notre manière de travailler, avec sécurité, respect de l'environnement et le souci des communautés qui nous accueillent. C'est dans cet esprit, et par solidarité, que nous avons répondu à la sollicitation en appuyant les actions de l'Agence nationale de l'assainissement et de la salubrité publique, l'ANASP» Il a également réaffirmé la volonté de Vivo Energy Guinée de demeurer un partenaire engagé auprès des institutions et des communautés, soulignant l'importance du dialogue et de la collaboration entre les secteurs public et privé pour relever ensemble les défis du pays. Une mobilisation collective portée par la Chambre des Mines de Guinée Cette contribution s'inscrit dans la continuité de la mobilisation engagée par la Chambre des Mines de Guinée dès la fin du mois de septembre, en réponse à l'appel des autorités du pays. En réceptionnant le don au nom de la Chambre des Mines de Guinée, son Directeur Exécutif, M. François Phopho Kamano, a salué la contribution de Vivo Energy Guinée à cet effort collectif. Au nom du Président du Conseil d'Administration, il a exprimé sa gratitude envers l'entreprise, soulignant que cette mobilisation traduit l'engagement sociétal des membres de la Chambre et leur volonté d'accompagner les pouvoirs publics. Un appui logistique pour renforcer les opérations d'assainissement Le Directeur Général de l'ANASP, M. Mamoudou Diané, a mis en avant l'importance de cet appui pour assurer la poursuite des opérations de gestion des déchets, dans un contexte où la fermeture de la décharge de Dar-es-Salam a profondément affecté le dispositif d'assainissement de Conakry. En s'exprimant au nom du Ministre en charge de l'Assainissement, il a salué la réponse apportée par les acteurs économiques à l'appel des autorités et adressé ses remerciements à Vivo Energy Guinée, à ses collaborateurs ainsi qu'à la Chambre des Mines de Guinée pour leur contribution. La Primature salue l'engagement du secteur privé dans l'effort national d'assainissement Monsieur Thierno Souleymane Diallo, Conseiller chargé de la Coordination interministérielle et du Suivi des réformes, a exprimé la reconnaissance du Gouvernement envers Vivo Energy Guinée et la Chambre des Mines de Guinée pour leur mobilisation. Il a rappelé que cet élan de solidarité fait suite à l'appel lancé par le Chef du Gouvernement au lendemain du drame de Dar-es-Salam, soulignant la nécessité d'une action concertée entre les pouvoirs publics et les acteurs économiques pour faire face aux défis d'assainissement de la capitale. La présence de la délégation de la Primature à cette cérémonie témoigne de l'importance accordée à la mobilisation du secteur privé dans la réponse nationale à cette situation d'urgence. Une contribution au service de l'intérêt général Au-delà de la réponse immédiate à cette situation d'urgence, cette initiative illustre l'importance de la collaboration entre les institutions publiques et le secteur privé face aux enjeux environnementaux et sanitaires. À travers ce don et ses engagements en matière de responsabilité sociétale, Vivo Energy Guinée réaffirme sa volonté de soutenir les communautés, de contribuer à l'amélioration de leur cadre de vie et de participer durablement au développement de la Guinée.

items.title: 2027: Fubara playing active role in Rainbow Coalition – Wike
items.description: The Minister of the Federal Capital Territory (FCT), Mr Nyesom Wike, says Gov. Siminalayi Fubara of Rivers remains an integral and active part of the ruling political team. Wike stated this during a media chat in Abuja on Tuesday, dismissing insinuations that Gov. Siminalayi Fubara of Rivers has been sidelined in the political architecture of the state. According to him, the governor remains an integral and active part of the ruling political team. Addressing questions about Fubara’s current status and quiet disposition, Wike maintained that the governor’s perceived silence does not equate to exclusion or unhappiness. “Fubara has not been pushed aside. If you know him, he’s been a very quiet person. “He is fully a member of the Rainbow Coalition and fully playing his part in efforts to ensure the re-election of President Bola Tinubu in 2027,” he said. The minister revealed that the governor recently hosted a crucial, high-level strategic meeting at his residence attended by key stakeholders, underscoring his active involvement in the state’s political direction. “Do you know what it takes to hold a meeting in his house? For everybody to be there? “What matters most to Gov. Fubara is ensuring that his political family retains its influence and power moving forward,” he said. Speaking as the campaign coordinator for Rivers, Wike said lists of campaign committee members have been duly submitted, with Fubara slated to serve as one of the primary leaders. Reflecting on past political tensions in the state, Wike blamed external actors and ungrateful elements, including certain opposition governors for trying to drive a wedge between him and Fubara for political mileage. He, however, noted that despite external attempts to exploit the situation, mutual forgiveness and reconciliation have prevailed. Wike also touched on speculation regarding Fubara’s future political trajectory after his tenure, including potential federal appointments. While noting that he does not possess the constitutional prerogative to nominate ministers, Wike maintained an optimistic outlook on the governor’s standing. Wike reiterated that speculations regarding friction between him and the governor are unfounded, stressing that both leaders were actively working together to safeguard the state’s political stability. He explained that the Rainbow Coalition in River was engineered to unite different political factions across party lines—including members of the All Progressives Congress (APC) and other groups. He added that the goal was to champion a unified agenda under Tinubu and avoid destructive litigations that previously plagued the state. When pressed on how offices and candidacies were being shared among coalition members, Wike defended the strategy as a display of high-level political ingenuity that respects the peculiarities of different areas while maintaining team solidarity. “When you talk about politicians that agree to form an umbrella, the umbrella does not mean that all the candidates will be one party. “We look at the peculiarities of areas, and say, listen, all of us are together and all of us are supporters of Mr President,” he said. items.title: STPT: ‘Sudan’s warring parties bypass sanctions through business networks’
items.description: A new report by the Sudan Transparency and Policy Tracker urges international governments to target the commercial networks and overseas partners sustaining the war. Sudan’s warring parties continue to circumvent international sanctions through overseas business networks, associated companies and alternative arms suppliers, according to a new report by the Sudan Transparency and Policy Tracker (STPT) . The report, Bypassing Sanctions, Sustaining the War Economy , published in October 2026, examines sanctions imposed since the war began in April 2023. It finds that restrictions have disrupted some financial and procurement channels but have failed to dismantle the wider networks financing the Sudanese Armed Forces (SAF) and the paramilitary Rapid Support Forces (RSF). The assessment identifies gaps in sanctions targeting SAF-linked companies, including the military-owned Zadna International Company for Investment, which it says has shifted much of its business towards Egypt and Gulf states and positioned itself to benefit from post-war reconstruction. The report also traces how the RSF-linked Al Junaid conglomerate generates revenue through gold trading networks, including routes that move gold from Sudan through South Sudan to the United Arab Emirates (UAE). Meanwhile, the report documents efforts by the SAF to secure alternative weapons suppliers, including Pakistan, and to develop domestic arms production using imported materials that can be harder to track. However, the authors caution that evidence of alternative procurement routes does not, by itself, prove that sanctions caused these shifts. The STPT argues that targeting individual companies is insufficient when their subsidiaries, joint ventures and commercial partners remain outside sanctions regimes. It urges governments to coordinate designations, strengthen enforcement and engage regional partners, particularly Egypt and Gulf states, to disrupt the networks sustaining the war. The report concludes that sanctions alone cannot end the conflict and must form part of a broader political strategy, alongside stronger regional cooperation and measures to limit harm to civilians. Football : YellowBet soutient la détection des jeunes talents de Foot Élite à Conakry
items.description: La première édition du tournoi de détection des jeunes talents, organisée par Foot Élite à l’initiative de l’ancien international guinéen Fodé Mansaré, a été lancée ce mardi 13 octobre 2026 au stade de Coléah, à Conakry. Sponsorisé par YellowBet Guinée, ce rendez-vous réunit de jeunes footballeurs issus de plusieurs académies du pays, en présence de recruteurs venus notamment de France. Jusqu’au 17 octobre prochain, les participants auront l’occasion de démontrer leurs qualités techniques et leur potentiel, dans l’espoir d’attirer l’attention de professionnels du recrutement. Parmi eux figure Boudjemaa Sharaf, recruteur de l’US Nancy, club évoluant en deuxième division française, qui a assisté aux premières rencontres de la compétition. À l’issue de cette première journée, le recruteur français s’est dit satisfait de ses premières observations, tout en soulignant que les jeunes joueurs avaient besoin d’un peu de temps pour se libérer sur le terrain. « Pour l’instant, ça se passe bien. Les joueurs sont un tout petit peu timides au commencement, mais c’est souvent comme ça. C’est une bonne impression pour l’instant », a-t-il confié. Pour sa première visite en Guinée, Boudjemaa Sharaf affirme ne pas rechercher un profil prédéfini. Son objectif est plutôt de repérer les joueurs dont les qualités pourraient répondre aux attentes de son club. « On cherche de tout. Il n’y a pas de profil particulier. S’il y a un joueur qui est bon, qui nous intéresse, on va le remarquer, le suivre et le faire venir », a-t-il expliqué. Le recruteur a également invité les jeunes footballeurs à persévérer dans leurs efforts et à continuer de travailler pour progresser. « Qu’ils continuent à travailler, qu’ils s’accrochent. Tout est possible dans la vie », a-t-il lancé, tout en saluant le potentiel footballistique de la Guinée. Fodé Mansaré veut offrir de nouvelles perspectives aux jeunes talents À l’origine de cette initiative, l’ancien international guinéen Fodé Mansaré entend rapprocher les jeunes footballeurs du pays des recruteurs susceptibles de leur ouvrir les portes du football professionnel. La présence de professionnels étrangers représente, à ses yeux, une étape importante dans la concrétisation de cette ambition. « Je suis très content que notre ami soit là, parce que c’est ça qu’on attendait depuis un bon moment. Pour organiser un tournoi ici, c’est tellement compliqué, c’est difficile », a-t-il reconnu. Pour l’ancien international, la réussite de cette première édition ne se mesurera pas uniquement au nombre de joueurs inscrits ou de recruteurs présents, mais surtout aux opportunités concrètes qui pourront en découler. « Si on arrive à détecter un joueur, voire deux ou trois, c’est le plus important », a-t-il insisté, espérant que cette compétition permettra à certains jeunes Guinéens de franchir un cap dans leur carrière. Au-delà de la détection, Fodé Mansaré souhaite également mettre en lumière le potentiel des joueurs formés en Afrique et rappeler que les talents ne se trouvent pas exclusivement en Europe. « On a des talents ici aussi. Ce n’est pas parce qu’on attend l’Europe, l’Europe, l’Europe qu’on doit oublier qu’il y a des talents chez nous », a-t-il souligné, invitant les jeunes à faire leurs preuves sur le terrain et à faire preuve de sérieux dans leur progression. YellowBet, un partenaire de la promotion du football jeune Le soutien de YellowBet Guinée constitue un apport important pour l’organisation de cette première édition du tournoi de détection de Foot Élite. En accompagnant cette initiative, le sponsor contribue à offrir une vitrine aux jeunes footballeurs guinéens et à favoriser leur mise en relation avec des professionnels du recrutement. Prévu jusqu’au 17 octobre, ce tournoi ambitionne ainsi de faire émerger de nouveaux talents et de leur donner l’occasion de se faire remarquer au-delà des frontières guinéennes.

items.title: Casablanca : une tonne de tabac de contrebande saisie, deux suspects arrêtés
items.description: Deux hommes âgés de 26 et 52 ans ont été interpellés, mardi 13 octobre, à Casablanca, en possession d’une tonne de tabac de contrebande. Une enquête judiciaire a été ouverte pour déterminer les circonstances de cette affaire et identifier d’éventuelles ramifications. Les éléments de la police judiciaire relevant de la zone de sûreté Rahma, à Casablanca, ont arrêté, aux premières heures de la matinée du mardi 13 octobre, deux individus soupçonnés d’être impliqués dans la détention et la commercialisation de tabac de contrebande. Les deux suspects ont été appréhendés en flagrant délit alors qu’ils transportaient et commercialisaient du tabac en poudre de contrebande à bord d’un camion destiné au transport de marchandises. Les opérations de fouille menées dans le cadre de cette intervention ont permis la saisie d’une quantité totale d’une tonne de cette substance. Les deux mis en cause ont été placés en garde à vue dans le cadre de l’enquête judiciaire menée sous la supervision du parquet compétent. Les investigations visent à établir l’ensemble des circonstances de cette affaire et à identifier les éventuelles ramifications de cette activité illicite. items.title: State security prosecution renews detention of 6 Matsda2sh journalists for 15 days
items.description: The detention of six journalists from fact-checking platform Matsda2sh was renewed for 15 days on Tuesday evening, pending further investigations, according to their lawyers. The renewal was ordered by the Supreme State Security Prosecution during today’s hearing in Case 8083/2026. The journalists Mohamed Ashraf Abu Emaira, Abdallah Kadry, Islam Barakat, Mohamed Adel, Mohamed Mahmoud and Omar Helal are being investigated in the case, registered with the Supreme State Security Prosecution, and were questioned again by prosecutors in sessions on Tuesday. The journalists’ lawyers told Mada Masr that questioning began around 1 pm and continued into the evening at the prosecution’s headquarters in the Fifth Settlement. The sessions revisited previous lines of questioning, including questioning about wages, the managerial structure of the platform and the way work was organized, with no new evidence presented to the journalists. All six journalists have been held at Badr 1 Prison since they were brought before the prosecution early last week. Their lawyers said they are due to receive their first family visits starting Thursday, as well as to be granted dedicated time for exercise. Security forces arrested the six Matsda2sh journalists in the span of24 hours during a campaign launched on September 28 which targeted the fact-checking platform’s team across several governorates. Their whereabouts remained unknown for five days, during which they were denied access to their lawyers and prevented from contacting their families, in violation of the counterterrorism law under which they were detained, according to EIPR . They appeared before the Supreme State Security Prosecution on October 4 when investigations began. The prosecution is investigating the six journalists for several offenses, including joining a terrorist group, spreading false news, misusing social media and receiving foreign funding. Several journalists told prosecutors during their interrogations that they had been subjected to torture and forced to record video footage in custody of themselves reading fabricated confessions, according to the Egyptian Initiative for Personal Rights, whose legal team is leading their defense. The Journalists Syndicate subsequently filed a complaint with the prosecutor general, calling for an investigation into allegations that the journalists were tortured at National Security Agency facilities before being brought before the prosecution. The Interior Ministry denied the allegations two hours after the syndicate issued its statement. Three of the detained journalists were referred to the Forensic Medicine Authority on October 6. The prosecution said the following day that forensic reports found no injuries on their bodies or signs of violence having been used against them. EIPR responded to the prosecutor’s statement by noting that prosecutors had refused to hear the journalists’ testimony as victims in the torture complaints they filed against the officers responsible for their detention at National Security Agency facilities. EIPR also said the prosecution had not summoned or heard testimony from the officers named in the complaints or witnesses to the incidents. It also noted that the journalists had not claimed to have visible injuries but had reported being subjected to torture, ill-treatment, threats and physical and psychological coercion. The post State security prosecution renews detention of 6 Matsda2sh journalists for 15 days first appeared on Mada Masr .

items.title: PM Shehbaz, EU official discuss Pakistan's efforts to curb migrant smuggling
items.description: ISLAMABAD: European Union Commissioner for Internal Affairs and Migration Magnus Brunner called on Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif on Tuesday to discuss strengthening Pakistan-EU cooperation in migration and mobility, one of the eight pillars of the Pakistan-EU Strategic Engagement Plan 2019. Welcoming Commissioner Brunner on his first visit to Pakistan, the prime minister underscored the importance Pakistan attaches to its partnership with the EU, according to a press release by the Prime Minister’s Office (PMO). The premier highlighted Pakistan’s sustained efforts to curb irregular migration and combat migrant smuggling and human trafficking through legislative reforms, institutional strengthening, effective enforcement and international cooperation. He reaffirmed Pakistan’s commitment to further strengthening cooperation across all pillars of the Pakistan-EU Strategic Engagement Plan. PM Shehbaz emphasised that efforts to address irregular migration should be complemented by practical opportunities for safe, orderly and regular migration. He noted that expanding legal pathways for Pakistani skilled workers and professionals would help meet the labour market needs of European countries while reducing prospective migrants’ vulnerability to smuggling networks. Brunner appreciated the measures taken and cooperation extended by the government of Pakistan, the PMO said. He expressed confidence that these efforts would contribute to expanding legal migration pathways and promoting mutually beneficial labour mobility between Pakistan and the European Union. President Zardari calls for more legal migration opportunities Brunner also called on President Asif Ali Zardari at the President’s House today, according to a two-part statement issued by the official presidential account on social media. “The meeting focused on Pakistan-EU relations, cooperation on migration management, efforts to combat human trafficking and migrant smuggling, and opportunities to facilitate legal migration,” the statement said. President Zardari called for greater opportunities for legal migration for Pakistani workers and professionals in Europe. He emphasised that Pakistan’s sustained efforts to curb irregular migration should be matched by “expanded legal pathways, skills-based mobility and structured cooperation” with the EU. He said that Pakistan attached great importance to its cooperation with the EU and reaffirmed the country’s commitment to implementing the Pakistan-EU Strategic Engagement Plan. The president highlighted the cooperation between the two countries in curbing irregular migration, noting that Pakistan continued to implement the EU Readmission Agreement and had readmitted more than 30,000 individuals over the years. He stressed the country’s commitment to combating human trafficking and irregular migration through “stronger legislation, institutional capacity, border controls and international cooperation”, the statement said. The president noted that, according to EU figures, irregular migration from Pakistan reduced by 64 per cent in the last 18 months, making it the only country in the region to achieve such a reduction. He said this progress reflected Pakistan’s “sustained efforts” and underlined the importance of expanding safe and legal avenues for migration. According to the president’s office, the meeting was informed that Pakistan had sought the EU’s assistance in strengthening the capacity of the Pakistan Coast Guards and the Federal Investigation Agency (FIA) to enhance efforts to combat irregular migration and migrant smuggling. “The president emphasised that legal migration pathways are essential to providing safe opportunities for workers and reducing reliance on smuggling networks,” the statement added. He highlighted the Pakistan-EU Migration and Mobility Dialogue as a “useful framework for matching Pakistan’s human-resource potential with European labour-market needs”, and expressed the hope that the next round of dialogue — expected to take place in Brussels early next year — would advance this cooperation. He expressed the country’s readiness to work with the EU on a structured mechanism to match its workforce with European labour-market requirements. President Zardari also welcomed the expansion of the EU Talent Partnerships framework and called for greater opportunities for skilled workers and professionals, including through circular migration. He expressed the hope that, given this partnership and the country’s efforts to curb irregular migration, the EU would consider establishing a European Legal Gateway Office in Pakistan. He said Pakistan and the EU have a “broad-based relationship spanning political dialogue, trade, development cooperation and other areas of mutual interest”, the statement added. He expressed confidence that continued engagement would strengthen mutual understanding and help advance practical cooperation on migration and mobility. Commissioner Brunner appreciated Pakistan’s role in maintaining regional balance and said Pakistan has done an “amazing job” in this regard, the statement noted. He also commended Pakistan’s efforts to prevent irregular migrants from undertaking dangerous journeys that cost many of them their lives. The commissioner was accompanied by EU Ambassador to Pakistan Raimundas Karoblis; Director for Migration and Home Affairs of the European Commission Henrik Nielsen; and member of Brunner’s cabinet, Grigorios Delavekouras. Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi, Minister of State for Interior Talal Chaudhry, Senator Sherry Rehman, Senator Saleem Mandviwalla and former federal minister Naveed Qamar also attended the meeting, the statement added. Dar meets commissioner, highlights efforts to curb irregular migration The EU commissioner also met with Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar in Islamabad, during which the deputy premier highlighted Pakistan’s efforts to curb irregular migration and combat migrant smuggling and human trafficking, the Foreign Office (FO) said. He stressed that these efforts should be complemented by greater opportunities for legal migration for Pakistani skilled workers and professionals. According to a statement issued by the FO, Dar expressed satisfaction with the positive momentum in Pakistan–EU relations. “The two sides discussed ways to strengthen cooperation on migration and mobility, a key pillar of the Pakistan–EU Strategic Engagement Plan (2019),” the FO said. It added that Brunner appreciated Pakistan’s progress in curbing irregular migration and noted the scope for expanding legal pathways for migration. Dar reaffirmed Pakistan’s commitment to further strengthening its partnership with the EU. He expressed the hope that Brunner’s visit would lead to “practical outcomes that benefit both sides”, the statement added. Naqvi, EU commissioner discuss border security Separately, Brunner also met with Interior Minister Naqvi in Islamabad, where they discussed enhancing cooperation in border security, legal migration and border management. The meeting was followed by delegation-level talks. Brunner appreciated Pakistan’s measures against illegal migration, describing the 64pc reduction in illegal migration to Europe resulting from the country’s efforts as commendable. He said the Federal Investigation Agency (FIA) had demonstrated professional competence despite limited resources, which was commendable. He added that the decline in illegal migration would pave the way for legal migration. Naqvi said Pakistan had adopted a zero-tolerance policy towards illegal migration. “After a 64pc reduction in illegal migration, our next target is its complete elimination,” the interior minister said, describing illegal migration as a serious global issue. The two sides also discussed the promotion of legal migration and enhancing opportunities for skilled workers between Pakistan and the European Union. Both sides agreed to further strengthen cooperation in immigration, institutional coordination and border management, and to work together on the EU’s Eastern Corridor Initiative to eliminate illegal migration. They also discussed increasing mutual cooperation to enhance the capacity of Pakistan Coast Guards and agreed to increase collaboration to promote border security and legal migration. Brunner assured Pakistan of all possible cooperation in this regard. The meeting was attended by the interior secretary, special and additional interior secretaries, FIA director general, Federal Constabulary inspector general, NCCIA director general, passports director general, Islamabad chief commissioner and other officials. Last month, Naqvi said Pakistan had recorded a 64pc reduction in illegal migration to Europe, describing the achievement as challenging despite limited resources. He said Pakistan’s next target was to eliminate illegal migration completely, stressing the need to expand legal migration opportunities, adopt modern technology and strengthen institutional capacity. In February, Pakistan and three European countries — Italy, Spain and Greece — reached a consensus on promoting legal pathways to “effectively combat illegal migration”. The three countries endorsed Naqvi’s proposal to establish legal pathways as a strategy to combat illegal migration and human smuggling during a conference.

items.title: PTI's Ali Zafar terms governor's rule in KP 'political crisis disguised as security solution'; ministers defend move
items.description: ISLAMABAD: Treasury and opposition members in the Senate debated the governor’s rule in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa on Tuesday, with PTI’s Barrister Ali Zafar terming the development a “political crisis disguised as a security solution” while federal ministers defended the move. The Centre on Sunday imposed governor’s rule in KP and emergency in 12 of its districts, citing the PTI-led provincial government’s “deliberate disengagement” from the fight against terrorism. The proclamations now require Parliament’s approval. It was against this backdrop that National Assembly and Senate sessions were convened on Tuesday. In the Senate, PTI’s Parliamentary Leader in the Senate Barrister Ali Zafar remarked that what was happening in KP was not merely an administrative decision but a “test of Pakistan’s Constitution”. “The Constitution must be our shield in a crisis, not a casualty of the crisis. The question is: are we using the Constitution to protect Pakistan, or are we using an emergency to change the political order of Pakistan?” he said. Zafar said no political party or patriotic Pakistani wanted terrorism to flourish and that terrorism must be defeated with full strength. “But we must defeat terrorism without allowing the fight against terrorism to become a fight against constitutional democracy,” he said. Referring to the constitutional provisions related to governor’s rule and emergency, he said Article 232 was to be employed in the situation of emergency and not as a “political weapon”. Similarly, Article 234 provided for extraordinary arrangements intended for extraordinary circumstances, he added. “Their existence does not mean they could be exercised without limits. The government must demonstrate that the constitutional conditions [for emergency and governor’s rule] have genuinely been met, that the action is necessary and proportionate, and that every applicable procedure has been followed. The existence of an emergency power does not place its exercise above the Constitution,” he said. Zafar further argued that the Centre could not simply declare that a provincial government could no longer function constitutionally and treat that declaration as the end argument. The legal basis, evidence, scope and consequences must withstand scrutiny, and courts must remain free to determine legality, he asserted. “If the government’s case is that terrorism has created an extraordinary situation in particular districts, it must explain why its response extended to the entire province and what safeguards protected the rest,” he added. The PTI alleged that “this is a political crisis disguised as a security solution”, pointing to the timing of the measure that came amid heightened political tensions and a breakdown of the dialogue between the government and the opposition, including the PTI, in the Centre. “You cannot restore public confidence by making people believe that their elected mandate can be taken away in the name of security,” he said. Zafar said the issue concerned provincial autonomy, federalism, elected representation, fundamental rights and the balance between the federation and its units. “Once extraordinary powers are normalised against one political opponent, no province and no party can assume it will never be the next one. Today it may be KP; tomorrow the precedent may be used elsewhere,” he warned. Calling on the Senate not to become a “rubber stamp”, he said Parliament, which represented the federation and gave every province an equal voice, must examine legal grounds, demand evidence and scrutinise necessity and proportionality for the measures in KP. “You may control the administration, but you cannot command democratic legitimacy. You may suspend a government, issue notifications and deploy the machinery of the state, but you cannot manufacture public trust by force. “If emergency is genuinely about protecting citizens, prove it through lawful, targeted and accountable action. If it becomes an instrument to suppress an elected mandate, the damage will outlast this government,” he said. Zafar added, “The Constitution is not an obstacle to national security; it is the foundation of national security. Break that foundation in the name of protecting Pakistan, and you may win control for a day but you will weaken the state for years to come.” Leader of the Opposition in Senate Raja Nasir Abbas termed Oct 11, when emergency and governor’s rule was imposed in KP, a “black day”, ruing celebrations by the “champions of democracy over the removal of a democratic government elected with two-thirds majority”. He maintained that an agreement between the Centre and the opposition had been reached on political issues, claiming that differences arose over linking security issues with political issues. He warned that “unnecessary violence” created hatred against the state among youth and urged the immediate withdrawal of the imposition of governor’s rule and emergency, as well as the resolution of issues through dialogue. Political matters could have been resolved by giving more time to negotiations, he added. Ministers defend governor’s rule For his part, Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi maintained that imposition of governor’s rule and emergency in KP was not in violation of the Constitution. “The PML-N and PPP sat together and examined every clause to ensure that no provision was violated,” he said, adding that the decision was not an easy one. He said talks between the Centre and the opposition had focused on terrorism from the first day. The minister added that the Centre had contacted the PTI leadership, including party Chairman Barrister Gohar Khan, on Oct 10, asking him to suggest amendments in the draft that was to be signed between the two sides after the talks. “Had an agreement been reached, this step would not have been taken,” he said. Naqvi said the government made six amendments in the draft, which was sent to KP Chief Minister Sohail Afridi, who has become non-functional as the provincial chief executive following the imposition of governor’s rule. The interior minister alleged that Afridi forwarded the draft to PTI leader Murad Saeed, after which the matter was “sabotaged”. Referring to security situation in KP, he said law enforcement and security personnel were laying down their lives while the “chief minister was delivering speeches against them”. He alleged that some in the PTI were in “contact with the Taliban and the Tehreek-i-Taliban Pakistan”, adding that evidence of this would be presented when required. Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar also spoke in the House, saying that the federal cabinet had “rightly decided” last week to end the process of political reconciliation with the PTI. He stressed that the PPP and PML-N had both made efforts to reach a point of understanding with the PTI. Regarding arguments that terrorism was also prevalent in Balochistan while emergency and governor’s rule were only in KP, he highlighted that the Balochistan government was “fully on board” with the Centre in fighting terrorism. “Whatever has happened is according to the law and Constitution,” he contented. Parliament approval for governor’s rule President Asif Ali Zardari had on Sunday issued proclamations of emergency and governor’s rule under Articles 232 and 234 of the Constitution, respectively. According to Article 232, in case the president “acts on his own” — which was not the case for KP as he acted on PM Shehbaz’s advice — the proclamation of emergency is to be placed before both houses of Parliament for approval by each house within 10 days. It also empowers Parliament “to make laws for a province, or any part thereof, with respect to any matter not enumerated in the Federal Legislative List” during emergency. Meanwhile, a proclamation for governor’s rule issued under Article 234 “shall be laid before a joint sitting and shall cease to be in force at the expiration of two months, unless before the expiration of that period it has been approved by resolution of the joint sitting and may by like resolution be extended for a further period not exceeding two months at a time”. In the upper house, Senator Kamran Murtaza of the Jamiat Ulemai-i-Islam–Fazl (JUI-F) had submitted a resolution on Monday opposing the imposition of governor’s rule in KP. NA session An NA session was also held on Tuesday, but concluded without any significant development. When the session began at around 7pm, NA Speaker Ayaz Sadiq administered the oath of membership to PML-N’s Malik Munir Iqbal Channar, who won the Bahawalpur polls last month held to fill the seat of his late father Malik Muhammad Iqbal Channar. Lawmakers then offered prayers for late MNA Chaudhry Mahmood Bashir Virk, who died last month after a prolonged illness. As MNAs from various parties took their turns to recall the services of Virk, there was slight commotion, which prompted the speaker to urge PTI Chairman Gohar Ali Khan to respect the late MNA. Gohar remarked that sessions are usually adjourned after prayers for a deceased member. Referring to the governor’s rule in KP, he said the “funeral of this house was also held on Oct 11”. “We tried to give you very much in dialogue, but you (PTI) were not ready to take what we had offered,” the speaker replied, then switched off Gohar’s mic. The speaker said political discussion will not be allowed today, but tomorrow (Wednesday). PPP’s Syed Naveed Qamar also urged the PTI chairman to acknowledge the services of Virk, who had stood by the Constitution. He said the PTI could raise its issues later as well. Lawmakers then continued to pay tribute to Virk, with Defence Minister Khawaja Asif and Planning Minister Ahsan Iqbal among those who highlighted his professional life. The proceedings were then adjourned till 11am on Wednesday. PTI seeks production orders for 9 MNAs Earlier in the day, the PTI requested the NA speaker to issue production orders for its nine “detained” MNAs ahead of NA and Senate sessions on Tuesday. In a letter to NA Speaker Sadiq, Chief Whip Amir Dogar claimed that the nine MNAs were “currently detained” and requested him to issue production orders for them to enable them to attend the 30th session starting today. The lawmakers comprised Haji Imtiaz Ahmad Choudhry (ΝΑ-68), Muhammad Jamal Ahsan Khan (NA-89), Mian Ghous Muhammad (ΝΑ-170), Sanaullah Khan Mastikhel (NΑ-91), Dawar Khan Kundi (NA-43), Junaid Akbar (NA-09), Amjad Ali Khan (NA-02), Fazal Muhammad Khan (ΝΑ-25) and Adil Khan Bazai (NA-262). “As the speaker of the National Assembly of Pakistan, the impartiality of your esteemed office requires that production orders be issued for all detained members, irrespective of their political affiliation, to ensure that no constituency remains unrepresented during the proceedings of the House,” the letter read. It requested Sadiq to issue the production orders under Rule 108 of the 2007 Rules of Procedure and Conduct of Business in the National Assembly.

items.title: 2027: INEC meets security agencies, party leaders, others in Lagos
items.description: The Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) in Lagos State on Tuesday met with security agencies, political parties and other stakeholders to strengthen collaboration and ensure peaceful conduct of the 2027 General Elections. Speaking at the stakeholders’ meeting in Lagos, Prof Ayobami Salami, Resident Electoral Commissioner (REC), said the meeting also aimed at mobilising public support for effective implementation of the commission’s electoral plans. Salami said the commission was intensifying preparations in logistics, personnel deployment, election security, voter education and accessibility. He said INEC had moved from strategic planning to active operational implementation, with nine of the 14 scheduled milestones for the 2027 elections already accomplished as of Oct. 6. “At the national level, the Register of Voters currently stands at approximately 103 million. “Preparations are also advancing in critical areas, including the procurement and delivery of 57,000 additional Bimodal Voter Accreditation System (BVAS) devices, software upgrades, battery optimisation and biometric calibration. “Similarly, extensive logistical arrangements are being made for the deployment of over 100,000 vehicles and 4,000 boats nationwide,” he said. The REC added that recruitment of approximately 1.4 million election personnel through the INECPRES portal was ongoing, with the application window scheduled to close on Nov. 18. He said Lagos, with 7,488,633 registered voters, remained strategically important to the electoral process, requiring meticulous planning and coordinated deployment of resources across its 20 Local Government Areas (LGAs). According to him, the state has 245 Registration Areas and 13,325 Polling Units, making effective logistics and inter-agency cooperation essential to the successful conduct of the elections. Salami said the commission was taking account of Lagos’ peculiar challenges, including traffic congestion, densely populated communities, commercial activities, difficult-to-access settlements and riverine locations. “Beyond these figures are the distinctive operational realities of Lagos: a large and mobile population, densely populated urban communities, extensive commercial activities, traffic challenges, some difficult-to-access settlements and riverine locations. “These peculiarities demand careful planning and solutions tailored to the circumstances of individual communities. “Our commitment is to ensure that these challenges are anticipated and addressed through timely, coordinated and effective operational arrangements,” he said. He said preparations included transportation planning, timely deployment of election materials, activation of Registration Area Centres (RACs) and assessment of the readiness of election personnel and facilities. The REC added that INEC was strengthening internal coordination and monitoring mechanisms to identify potential operational challenges early and address them before they affected election activities. He said the commission would also provide assistive materials, including Braille ballot guides, EC30 PWD posters and magnifying glasses, where applicable, to promote participation by persons with disabilities. Salami urged organisations representing persons with disabilities to continue engaging with the commission and providing recommendations to improve accessibility and inclusion. On election security, he said INEC would continue working with relevant security agencies through the Inter-Agency Consultative Committee on Election Security (ICCES), led by the Nigeria Police Force, to identify and mitigate potential electoral risks. “Our collective priority is to safeguard voters, election personnel, observers, electoral materials and facilities throughout the electoral process. “Particular attention will be given to prevention of electoral violence, intimidation, vote-buying, ballot snatching and other unlawful activities capable of undermining the credibility of elections. “In collaboration with relevant law enforcement and anti-corruption agencies, appropriate preventive and enforcement measures will be pursued in accordance with the law,” he said. The REC called on political parties, candidates and their supporters to conduct their activities responsibly, respect electoral laws and avoid actions capable of disrupting public peace. He stressed that political competition should not be used to justify violence, intimidation or other unlawful conduct, adding that protecting citizens’ right to participate freely in elections was a shared responsibility. Salami also raised concerns about misinformation, disinformation and the misuse of artificial intelligence to circulate manipulated images, fabricated reports, synthetic audio and video recordings, deepfakes and voice clones. He urged political actors, media practitioners, civil society organisations and members of the public to verify election-related information through authorised INEC communication channels before sharing it. The REC reiterated that the collation and declaration of election results must follow established legal procedures and be undertaken only by duly authorised electoral officials. He said unverified figures and speculative reports should not be presented as official results, warning that false information could generate confusion, heighten political tensions and undermine public confidence in the electoral process. Salami emphasised that the successful conduct of the elections required the commitment of all stakeholders, noting that INEC could not achieve the objective of credible elections acting alone. “Political parties have a great responsibility to promote peaceful competition, respect electoral regulations and encourage responsible conduct among their members and supporters. “Security agencies must continue to provide a safe and enabling environment for electoral activities. “Traditional rulers, religious leaders, youth organisations, and community institutions remain important partners in promoting civic responsibility, peaceful coexistence and public participation,” he said. He also urged civil society organisations to intensify voter education and public enlightenment, while calling on the media to uphold accuracy, fairness and professionalism in reporting electoral activities. The REC appealed to stakeholders to encourage registered voters to verify their details on the Register of Voters, collect their Permanent Voter Cards, when available, and obtain electoral information from authorised sources. He said INEC remained committed to professionalism, transparency, inclusivity and effective implementation of its constitutional responsibilities as preparations for the 2027 General Elections gathered momentum. “Our objective is clear: to ensure that every stage of the electoral process is properly planned, effectively implemented and conducted in a manner that strengthens public confidence in the Commission and the integrity of elections. “With your continued cooperation, constructive engagement and shared commitment, I am confident that Lagos State can contribute significantly to the successful conduct of a peaceful, credible, transparent and inclusive General Elections,” he said. The post 2027: INEC meets security agencies, party leaders, others in Lagos appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Black Queens thrash Mauritius 7-0 to advance 10-0 on aggregate in Olympic Qualifiers
items.description: The Black Queens produced a scintillating performance to demolish Mauritius 7-0 in the second leg of the second round of qualifiers for the Los Angeles 2028 Olympic Games at the Essipong Stadium on Tuesday. The emphatic victory secures a 10-0 aggregate win for Ghana, having won the first leg 3-0 in Mauritius last Thursday. Head Coach Kim Lars Björkegren’s side dominated from start to finish, overwhelming the visitors with pace, power and precision in the final third. Captain Portia Boakye opened the scoring for the Queens before Evelyn Badu doubled the lead. Ajegipina Zakaria made it 3-0 for Ghana going into the break. After the recess, the Queens continued to pile pressure on Mauritius, with substitutes making an instant impact. Benedicte Simon marked her introduction with a goal in the 73rd minute, before Jennifer Cudjoe added the fifth in the 87th minute. Nancy Amoh and Mukarama Abdulai completed the rout with two late strikes to make it 7-0. The result underlines Ghana’s determination to secure a historic first qualification for the Women’s Olympic Football Tournament. With the win, Ghana progresses to the third round of the qualifiers in search of a ticket to LA 2028.

items.title: Govt reduces petrol price by Rs2.71 per litre, high-speed diesel rate by Re0.03
items.description: Pakistan fuel prices, 2026 Official ex-depot prices (PKR/litre) — OGRA & Ministry of Energy notifications Petrol (MS-92) Diesel (HSD) Pre-crisis baseline Source: OGRA / Ministry of Energy (Petroleum Division); Dawn.com · " style="width: 100%; min-height: 50px; max-height: 30000px; border: none; overflow: hidden; display: block;" scrolling="no"> The government on Tuesday reduced the price of petrol by Rs2.71 per litre, and that of high-speed diesel (HSD) by Rs0.03 per litre. Following the revision, petrol will retail at Rs392.66 per litre, while HSD will cost Rs396.82 per litre. The government continues to levy Rs114 per litre in taxes and duties on petrol and Rs100 per litre on diesel. According to the Petroleum Division’s notification, the new prices are applicable for Oct 14 (Wednesday). The price of HSD has come down from a peak of Rs520.35 recorded on April 3. Its price had started rising from Rs281 per litre after the US-Iran war broke out on February 28. The petrol price had peaked at Rs458.41 on April 3 after beginning its upward trajectory from Rs266 in the first week of March. Meanwhile, the government has reintroduced a raft of austerity measures in response to rising fuel prices amid the ongoing Middle East conflict. Under these measures, markets are required to close by 9pm and fuel allocations for official vehicles has been cut by 50 per cent for three months. On September 13, Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif also announced a “ relief scheme ” for users of motorcycles, autos and vehicles of up to 800cc to “alleviate the burden” of rising global oil prices. Previously, on July 17, Petroleum Minister Ali Pervaiz Malik announced that fuel prices would now be fixed on a daily basis due to fluctuations in international market prices following renewed hostilities between Iran and the US. Prior to this, the government had been announcing weekly revisions to fuel prices since early March, alongside measures for the conservation of fuel amid possible oil supply disruptions due to the ongoing conflict in the Middle East. The federal government in April also announced targeted relief measures to provide subsidised fuel. The petroleum minister stated that the cabinet and the prime minister had decided to give the Oil and Gas Regulatory Authority (Ogra) the responsibility of deciding fuel prices on a daily basis based on international market trends. Petrol is mainly used in private transport, small vehicles, rickshaws and two-wheelers, and changes in its price affect the middle and lower-middle classes. Similarly, changes in diesel prices also impact the public at large, as it is mainly used in the heavy transport sector, power plants and large generators. Petrol and high-speed diesel (HSD) are the major revenue earners, with monthly sales of about 700,000 to 800,000 tonnes, compared to just 10,000 tonnes of monthly demand for kerosene.

items.title: Personnes déplacées : les enfants reprennent l’école, les familles cherchent encore un toit
items.description: a Mopti, des familles deplacees ont quitte les salles de classe avant la rentree, permettant aux cours de reprendre. a Bamako, les enfants de l'ancien site de Faladie sont progressivement reinscrits dans les ecoles. Mais derriere cette reprise, les conditions de logement des familles restent preoccupantes. La rentree peut se poursuivre, mais le quotidien reste difficile pour de nombreuses familles deplacees. a Djenedaga et a Kouakrou, dans la region de Mopti, les familles qui occupaient des salles de classe ont rejoint de nouveaux lieux d'hebergement. a Bamako, celles de l'ancien site de Faladie se sont dispersees dans plusieurs quartiers, compliquant parfois la scolarisation des enfants. a Mopti, les ecoles respirent, les familles cherchent encore des abris a Djenedaga, les salles de classe ont ete liberees avant la rentree. Une solution rendue possible grâce a la mobilisation du chef du village, Boyon Karabenta, et de ses conseillers. Certaines familles ont trouve refuge dans des maisons abandonnees ou mises a leur disposition. Mais pour d'autres, l'hebergement reste provisoire. Le retour dans les localites d'origine dependra notamment de l'evolution de la situation securitaire. En attendant, les familles doivent s'adapter a leurs nouvelles conditions de vie. Boubacar Thienta, porte-parole des deplaces, souligne que « le site initialement propose a Medina Coura ne repond pas a leurs besoins ». Principalement issus de la communaute bozo, ces deplaces souhaitent etre heberges pres du fleuve, essentiel a leurs activites et a leur mode de vie. a Bamako, les enfants retrouvent progressivement le chemin de l'ecole Depuis la dispersion de l'ancien site de Faladie, les familles se sont installees dans plusieurs quartiers peripheriques, notamment a Sirakoro et a Mountougoula. Pour les parents, il faut desormais trouver une ecole accessible a leurs enfants, parfois loin de leur nouveau domicile. Malgre ces contraintes, les inscriptions avancent. Selon Amadou Tamboura, enseignant volontaire, la grande majorite des enfants a deja ete inscrite ou fait l'objet de demarches. Les parents peuvent s'orienter vers differents etablissements : ecoles classiques, medersas, ecoles franco-arabes ou privees. Mais inscrire un enfant ne suffit pas toujours a garantir sa presence reguliere en classe. Le logement, les deplacements et les depenses du quotidien restent des obstacles pour ces familles. Au-dela de la rentree, le defi de la continuite scolaire La liberation des salles de classe a Mopti et les reinscriptions a Bamako permettent aux enfants de poursuivre leur scolarite. Mais pour les familles deplacees, une autre urgence demeure : trouver un hebergement adapte et stable. La rentree est donc une etape franchie, pas la fin des difficultes. Pour eviter de nouvelles interruptions scolaires, les enfants auront besoin de conditions de vie qui leur permettent de rester durablement a l'ecole. items.title: Kaizen as a strategic pathway for micro business scale-up in Ghana
items.description: Introduction Ghana’s economic landscape is overwhelmingly dominated by micro, small, and medium-sized enterprises (MSMEs), which constitute over 90 per cent of all registered businesses and provide approximately 80 per cent of total employment. Within this ecosystem, micro-sized businesses alone account for 90.4 per cent of all establishments, representing a significant rise from 16.6 per cent in 2014. These enterprises, often operating within the informal economy and driven predominantly by women and youth, contribute around 70 per cent of Ghana’s Gross Domestic Product. Despite their numerical dominance, micro businesses face persistent challenges in scaling up, including limited access to finance, inefficient production processes, and weak management systems. Kaizen, the Japanese philosophy of continuous improvement, has emerged as a transformative methodology for addressing these challenges. Since 2012, Ghana has actively promoted Kaizen practices to sustainably improve the quality and productivity of businesses. Through collaborative initiatives involving the Ghana Enterprises Agency (GEA), the United Nations Industrial Development Organization (UNIDO), and the Japan International Cooperation Agency (JICA), thousands of Ghanaian micro and small enterprises have been trained in Kaizen principles, with measurable improvements in productivity, product quality, and operational efficiency. This article examines what constitutes a micro business in Ghana and outlines seven strategic points through which Kaizen can be leveraged for scale-up. What Makes a Business a Micro Business in Ghana? The classification of micro enterprises in Ghana is governed by the Classification of MSMEs Regulation, which employs a combination of employment size, turnover, and asset value as defining criteria. According to the Ghana Enterprises Agency (GEA), through Legislative Instrument 2470, a micro enterprise is defined as a business with 1 to 5 permanent employees and either a fixed asset value or annual turnover not exceeding GH¢150,000. This definition aligns with the Ghana Statistical Service’s characterisation of micro enterprises as businesses employing between 1 and 5 workers. The regulatory framework further distinguishes micro enterprises from small enterprises, which employ 6 to 30 permanent employees and have either fixed assets or turnover ranging from GH¢150,000 to GH¢6,000,000. This differentiation is significant because it establishes clear thresholds that micro business owners can target as they pursue growth. Beyond the quantitative metrics, micro businesses in Ghana exhibit several distinctive characteristics. The Integrated Business Establishment Survey reveals that 92.3 per cent of businesses in Ghana remain informal, with the vast majority of micro enterprises operating outside formal regulatory frameworks. Many operate from non-traditional locations pavements, roadside stalls, and mobile setups rather than formal offices or shops. The sector is also characterised by significant income inequality, with approximately 31 per cent of operators earning GH¢100 or less per day. Small start-up capital, proximity to customers, and adaptability to market demand are key drivers of this sector. These characteristics collectively define the micro business landscape in Ghana and underscore both the vulnerabilities and the immense potential of this segment. It is within this context that Kaizen offers a structured yet accessible pathway for incremental growth and formalisation. Seven Strategic Points for Using Kaizen to Scale Up Workplace Organisation through 5S Principles The foundation of Kaizen implementation for micro businesses lies in the 5S methodology Sort, Set in Order, Shine, Standardise, and Sustain. This systematic approach to workplace organisation requires minimal financial investment, making it particularly suitable for resource-constrained micro enterprises. Research from JICA’s Kaizen projects in Ghana confirms that 5S is an initiative that “does not require much resource input and can be easily implemented by local industries that are dominated by micro and small companies”. The practical impact of 5S is evident in the experience of some businesses in an Agro-processing, small-scale gari-manufacturing outfit in Mampong, Ashanti Region. Where the owner has described how Kaizen transformed her operations: “In the past, our factory was distorted, and things were not well arranged. Now, we have compartmentalized our space and labelled each section accordingly. Currently, we have clearly demarcated areas such as the washing, peeling, processing and pressing units”. This reorganisation reduced movement time and improved daily output from one and a half bags to three bags. For micro businesses, such improvements in workspace efficiency directly translate to increased production capacity without the need for additional space or equipment. Waste Reduction and Process Optimisation Kaizen provides micro businesses with practical tools to identify and eliminate the seven types of waste: overproduction, waiting, transportation, over-processing, inventory, motion, and defects. This focus on waste reduction is particularly critical in Ghana, where many MSMEs lose significant inputs and raw materials during production due to unrefined processes. The experience of yet another business in the Garments space in Takoradi exemplifies this strategic advantage. After participating in Kaizen training under a UNIDO project in 2024, the owner identified significant inefficiencies in production, including poor tool organisation, unnecessary movement, and an unstructured factory layout. By reorganising workflows, introducing straight-line production, and assigning specialised tasks such as pattern cutting, the company reduced waste, increased output, and improved consistency. The productivity gains enabled reinvestment in new capabilities, including a fabric printing machine that reduced costs and improved quality control. Human Resource Development and Employee Engagement Kaizen’s emphasis on people, respecting employees, encouraging participation, and creating safe workplaces aligns well with the human-centric nature of micro businesses in Ghana. Research on Kaizen implementation in Ghana’s garment industry has identified workers’ training and development as a critical success factor, alongside leadership commitment and the physical work environment. The Garments business I just spoke about is a case that demonstrates how Kaizen can strengthen employee engagement. Visual target boards now track daily performance, while a suggestion box encourages staff to contribute ideas, reinforcing a culture of continuous improvement. As a result of these Kaizen-driven improvements, the workforce grew from 17 employees to 26, the majority of whom are women. For micro businesses operating with small teams, this approach not only enhances productivity but also improves employee retention and job satisfaction, factors that are critical for sustainable growth. Data-Driven Decision Making One of Kaizen’s most powerful contributions to micro business scale-up is the shift towards data-driven decision making. Many micro enterprises in Ghana operate on intuition and habit rather than systematic measurement, which limits their ability to identify improvement opportunities and track progress. The UNIDO Kaizen Expansion Project in Ghana introduced digital tools such as the Smart and Sustainable Agri-Business (SSAB) dashboard and U-SPARK technology, enabling enterprises to visualise and better manage their performance through real-time data collection on key performance indicators. More than 2,800 enterprises strengthened their capabilities in enterprise performance management through this project, with half of them women-led. For micro businesses, the ability to track productivity metrics, resource efficiency, and quality indicators provides a foundation for informed growth strategies. Quality Improvement and Standardisation Kaizen’s focus on quality improvement is directly linked to market access and competitiveness. Micro businesses that can consistently deliver quality products are better positioned to secure contracts with larger organisations, access formal markets, and command premium prices. The National Kaizen Awards in Ghana have recognised numerous micro and small enterprises that achieved remarkable quality improvements through Kaizen adoption. One such enterprise, a micro and small enterprise specialising in body soaps and creams, was named the overall winner of the 2024 National Kaizen Awards after winning the Micro and Small Enterprise category. The company’s CEO attributed the company’s operational improvements and increased productivity to the effective implementation of Kaizen practices. Other award winners have similarly demonstrated how Kaizen-driven quality improvements can catalyse business growth. Leadership Commitment and Strategic Focus For Kaizen to deliver transformative results in micro businesses, leadership commitment is essential. Research from Ghana’s garment production industry has identified leadership commitment as a critical success factor for Kaizen implementation, alongside workers’ training and development. Micro business owners must be willing to lead by example, allocate time for improvement activities, and sustain momentum over time. The Japan International Cooperation Agency’s Kaizen projects in Ghana have emphasised the importance of embedding Kaizen principles at the leadership level. One of my old colleagues at the Business Resource Centre once noted that “the Japanese government is highly committed to the growth and development of SMEs” and that this institutional commitment has been instrumental in creating effective support systems. For micro business owners in Ghana, adopting this mindset means treating Kaizen not as a one-time training event but as an ongoing management philosophy that guides daily operations and strategic decisions. Accessing Institutional Support and Networks Micro businesses in Ghana do not have to implement Kaizen in isolation. A robust ecosystem of support institutions, including the Ghana Enterprises Agency, JICA, UNIDO, and Business Resource Centres across the country provides training, technical assistance, and networking opportunities. The GEA operates more than 209 Business Advisory Centres across Ghana, providing business development support to enterprises outside the main commercial centres. The GEA has mainstreamed Kaizen into its core operations, training over 33,478 micro and small enterprises through initiatives such as the Mastercard Foundation’s Young Africa Works, the Ghana Jobs and Skills Project, on which i personally taught this in one of the modules, where I took over 800 participants in Ada East & Kpone Katamanso as the lead facilitator and the Bizbox Project. The ILO’s experience in Ghana further demonstrates that management training combining the Start and Improve Your Business (SIYB) programme with basic Kaizen elements significantly improves the performance of small firms. Micro business owners should actively seek out these institutional resources, which are often provided at minimal or no cost, as a strategic lever for scale-up. Conclusion: How Kaizen Has Driven Business Success in Ghana The evidence from Ghana’s experience with Kaizen demonstrates a clear pattern of success that positions this Japanese philosophy as a proven pathway for micro business scale-up. Since the launch of the UNIDO Kaizen Expansion Project in 2022, more than 200 enterprises have improved productivity, product quality, operational efficiency, and overall business performance. Over 2,800 enterprises, half of them women-led, strengthened their capabilities in enterprise performance management. A further 142 firms achieved improvements in productivity, energy efficiency, and waste reduction, while firms adopted 40 new technologies. The success of Kaizen in Ghana is rooted in several factors that make it particularly well-suited to the micro business context. First, Kaizen’s incremental, low-cost approach aligns with the resource constraints that characterise micro enterprises. Unlike expensive technology solutions or large-scale restructuring, Kaizen focuses on small, continuous improvements that can be implemented with existing resources. Second, Kaizen’s emphasis on human development and participation resonates with Ghana’s collectivist cultural values and the people-centred nature of micro businesses. Third, the institutional support ecosystem, including GEA, JICA, UNIDO, and the network of Business Resource Centres has made Kaizen accessible to businesses across all regions of Ghana. The transformative experiences of some Ghanaian businesses illustrate the tangible benefits of Kaizen adoption. Some grew their workforce from 17 to 26 employees, invested in new machinery, and improved product quality through Kaizen-driven process improvements. Others doubled their daily output from one and a half bags to three bags of gari through workplace organisation and process optimisation. Another rose from a micro enterprise to a national Kaizen award winner, demonstrating that scale-up is achievable through sustained commitment to continuous improvement. The call by Ghana’s Deputy Minister for Trade, Agribusiness and Industry to make Kaizen a permanent service within the GEA reflects the growing recognition that this approach is not merely a training programme but a strategic national asset. With GEA positioning itself as a regional centre of excellence for Kaizen in West Africa, the potential for micro businesses to leverage this methodology for growth has never been greater. For Ghanaian micro business owners, the message is clear: Kaizen offers a structured, practical, and proven pathway to scale up. By committing to continuous improvement, one small change at a time, micro enterprises can overcome the constraints that have historically limited their growth and position themselves for sustainable success in Ghana’s evolving economy. *** Kweku Hammond, Senior Sales & Marketing / Faculty, Nova Business School Africa

items.title: Shell to sell Nigeria domestic gas business to Vaaris Energy
items.description: By Faith Odukomaiya Shell Petroleum B.V. has signed an agreement to sell its full interest in Shell Nigeria Gas Group to Vaaris Energy Limited, a Nigerian energy company, as the oil major refocuses its investments on strategic businesses. Shell’s Country Chair in Nigeria, Elohor Aiboni, said the transaction would provide a platform for the domestic gas distribution business to grow under new ownership. “Shell Nigeria Gas has served industrial and commercial customers in Nigeria for more than 25 years, supported by the commitment and expertise of its people,” Aiboni said. “We believe this agreement provides a much stronger platform for the business’ next chapter under new ownership. Shell continues to focus on strategic Deepwater and Integrated Gas positions in Nigeria.” Established in 1998, Shell Nigeria Gas (SNG) supplies natural gas to industrial and commercial customers through about 170 kilometres of pipeline infrastructure across Ogun, Abia and Rivers states. It serves more than 130 connected customers. The transaction includes Shell Nigeria Gas Holding B.V., established in 2019, which holds all but one of the shares in Shell Nigeria Gas Limited. Shell said the sale was consistent with its strategy of simplifying its portfolio and concentrating investment on areas where it has competitive strengths. In Nigeria, the company will continue to focus on Deepwater and Integrated Gas, including its interest in Nigeria LNG. The proposed sale does not include Shell’s upstream gas production, liquefied natural gas (LNG) or international gas trading businesses. Vaaris Energy has interests across the oil and gas value chain and an existing operational presence in Nigeria. The transaction remains subject to regulatory conditions and approvals. Until completion, Shell Nigeria Gas Group will remain part of Shell and continue to serve its customers and operate as usual. The post Shell to sell Nigeria domestic gas business to Vaaris Energy appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Minister orders suspension of Obuasi SHS headmaster over alleged sexual misconduct following JoyNews investigation
items.description: The Minister of Education has directed the immediate suspension of the Headmaster of Obuasi Senior High Technical School, Zakaria Abdulai, over allegations of sexual misconduct involving a female student. According to a statement issued by the Ministry of Education, the directive follows an investigation by JoyNews and Manasseh Azure Awuni into the allegations against the headmaster. The Ministry said the Minister had instructed the Director-General of the Ghana Education Service (GES) to take immediate steps to suspend Mr Abdulai pending a full investigation into the matter. The Minister has also requested the Criminal Investigation Department (CID) Headquarters of the Ghana Police Service to commence investigations. The Ministry of Education and the GES reiterated their position that alleged misconduct of this nature would not be tolerated in educational institutions across the country. The statement, signed by the Ministry’s Press Secretary, Hashmin Mohammed, stressed that parents and guardians entrust their children to teachers, whose responsibility is to protect and safeguard them rather than abuse them. The suspension is intended to allow investigations into the allegations to proceed.

items.title: El Rey, en Ceuta: “La soberanía y la integridad territorial no son negociables y, ante cualquier riesgo, nuestra obligación es su defensa”
items.description: A última hora de la tarde de este martes, tras darse un baño de cariño y afecto por distintos puntos de la urbe de Ceuta, Felipe VI ha culminado su primera visita a la ciudad autónoma con un discurso muy contundente. Dentro del Parador Las Murallas, el Rey ha calificado de “violación de nuestra frontera” el cruce multitudinario de finales de julio, ha defendido la “soberanía” y “la integridad” de la ciudad autónoma, y ha subrayado la “obligación” de defenderlas. Todo dos meses y medio después de la entrada masiva que ha puesto en jaque a la urbe africana. El monarca ha reivindicado además su papel como “jefe del Estado”, algo que no suele hacer en este tipo de alocuciones, y ha mantenido que “la violación de nuestra frontera sigue teniendo un enorme impacto en España entera”. “No os vamos a dejar solos ni indefensos”, ha prometido a los ceutíes. También ha mencionado a Marruecos, con quien ha mostrado “la responsabilidad de mantener una buena relación de vecindad”, pero basado en los “respeto mutuos” entre ambos países. Felipe VI ha pronunciado sus primeras palabras a las 19.30 ante miembros de la sociedad civil ceutí convocados para el acto celebrado en el hotel, donde pernoctará esta noche antes de viajar mañana miércoles a Melilla, y en una sala donde ha sido recibido con el himno nacional y entre gritos de “¡Viva el Rey!”.
