items.description: Le Camarade Premier ministre, Chef du Gouvernement, Rimtalba Jean Emmanuel Ouédraogo, a reçu en audience, ce mardi 13 octobre 2026, à Ouagadougou, les ministres en charge de l’Enseignement supérieur des pays de l’Alliance des États du Sahel (AES) et du Togo. Cette audience s’inscrit dans le cadre de la deuxième Conférence des responsables des institutions d’enseignement supérieur et de recherche (IESR) de l’AES, qui se tient les 13 et 14 octobre dans la capitale burkinabè. ‎ ‎La délégation comprenait le ministre de l’Enseignement supérieur, de la Recherche et de l’Innovation technologique du Niger, le Pr Mamadou Saidou ; le ministre de l’Enseignement supérieur et de la Recherche scientifique du Mali, le Pr Bouréma Kansaye ; le ministre de l’Enseignement supérieur, de la Recherche et de l’Innovation du Burkina Faso, le Pr Adjima Thiombiano ; ainsi que le ministre délégué chargé de l’Enseignement supérieur et de la Recherche de la République togolaise, le Pr Gado Tchangbedji. ‎ ‎Placée sous le thème « Harmonisation et endogénéisation des systèmes d’enseignement supérieur, de recherche et d’innovation pour des ressources humaines compétentes et un développement harmonieux des pays de l’AES », cette conférence vise à consolider la coopération en matière de formation, de recherche et d’innovation. Le Togo y participe en qualité de pays invité. ‎ ‎Au cours de l’audience, le Camarade Premier ministre a salué la dynamique engagée et invité les ministres à faire de leurs échanges un levier de renforcement de l’AES. Tout en reconnaissant l’ampleur des défis, il a affirmé que le chemin emprunté est le bon. « L’envahisseur est parti, mais dans bien des domaines, c’est malheureusement nous-mêmes qui prolongeons sa présence. Il nous revient de prendre conscience pour apporter des solutions endogènes à nos difficultés », a déclaré le Chef du Gouvernement. ‎ ‎Dans cette perspective, le Camarade Premier ministre a appelé à l’endogénéisation des formations, afin de mieux répondre aux réalités et aux besoins des populations. Il a également salué la présence du Togo, qu’il a jugée légitime et souhaitable, soulignant que le savoir ne saurait être confiné à des frontières artificielles. ‎ ‎À l’issue de l’audience, le Pr Mamadou Saidou a indiqué que la délégation était venue présenter ses civilités au Chef du Gouvernement et lui faire le point sur les travaux de la conférence. Il a rappelé que cette deuxième édition prolonge les engagements pris à Bamako, en juin 2025, conformément à la volonté des trois chefs d’État de l’AES. Le ministre nigérien a salué la qualité des échanges ainsi que l’attention portée par le Camarade Premier ministre aux préoccupations des différents systèmes d’enseignement supérieur. ‎ ‎Pour sa part, le Pr Gado Tchangbedji a remercié les pays de l’AES pour l’invitation adressée au Togo. Il a souligné que cette initiative rejoint les orientations de son pays en matière d’intégration régionale et de développement commun. « Nous sommes fiers d’être présents à ces travaux parce qu’au-delà de l’intégration régionale, cela correspond à notre vision », a-t-il déclaré. ‎ ‎Évoquant l’expérience de certains pays asiatiques, le ministre togolais a insisté sur la nécessité, pour les États africains, de renforcer leurs capacités de formation et de recherche afin de mieux maîtriser leur développement. Cette ambition rejoint, a-t-il précisé, la nouvelle feuille de route du Togo, qui prévoit notamment le développement d’un capital humain productif et d’une recherche adaptée aux besoins nationaux. ‎ ‎La rencontre de Ouagadougou contribue à structurer la coopération entre les institutions d’enseignement supérieur et de recherche de l’AES. À travers cette concertation, les pays de la Confédération prennent à bras-le-corps un enjeu essentiel de leur souveraineté : former les compétences et produire les savoirs nécessaires pour maîtriser leur développement, en accord avec leurs valeurs et les aspirations de leurs peuples. ‎ ‎𝐃𝐂𝐑𝐏/𝐏𝐫𝐢𝐦𝐚𝐭𝐮𝐫𝐞

items.title: Army conducts successful test launch of hypersonic Fatah-2 extended range missile: ISPR
items.description: The Pakistan Army successfully test-launched the Fatah-2 extended range (ER) hypersonic ballistic missile, the military’s media wing said in a statement on Tuesday. According to Inter-Services Public Relations (ISPR), the Fatah-2 ER is equipped with advanced navigation and state-of-the-art avionics. “It is capable of engaging targets with high precision and defeating [the] enemy’s missile defence systems due to its unique trajectory and manoeuvrability features,” it added. “Fatah-2 ER, with its extended range, will further enhance [the] army’s reach and capability of engaging deep targets.” The test launch was witnessed by Army Rocket Force Command (ARFC) chief Lt Gen Nauman Zakaria, senior army officers, scientists and engineers. The ARFC commander “appreciated the dedication and technical prowess of scientists and engineers”, ISPR said. It further said the president, prime minister, and the chief of defence forces congratulated the scientists and engineers on the successful test launch of the “extended range version of Fatah-2 weapon system”. Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi congratulated the nation on the success of the test and termed it an important advancement in the defence sector. Last week, the indigenously developed extended version of the Fatah-IV ground-launched cruise missile also underwent a successful test launch . In a statement, ISPR said, “Equipped with advanced avionics and state-of-the-art navigational aids, the weapon system is capable of engaging targets at extended ranges with high precision and lethality.” “The test also validated additional technical parameters of various sub-systems incorporated for improved accuracy and enhanced survivability,” it added.

items.title: Obaasima Summit: ‘AI is not a spiritual attack’ — Rev. Dr. Ofori-Boateng urges young women to embrace technology
items.description: Young women have been urged to embrace artificial intelligence (AI) and continuous learning as technology reshapes the world, with an Anglican priest cautioning against interpreting AI as a spiritual threat. Director of Programmes for the Anglican Diocese of Accra, Rev. Dr. Akua Buabema Ofori-Boateng, gave the advice at the 2026 Obaasima Summit, where speakers encouraged young women to prepare for leadership and build on the achievements of previous generations. She said the rapid pace of technological change made lifelong learning essential for anyone seeking to remain relevant and effective in leadership. “Embrace lifelong learning. I hold many degrees, and I’m still learning,” she said. Rev. Dr. Ofori-Boateng stressed that academic qualifications should be viewed as the beginning, rather than the end, of the learning process. “Your education does not end when you walk across the stage and they hand you a certificate. It begins there because the world is changing rapidly, and those who lead the world never stop being students,” she said. Citing artificial intelligence as an example of a technology young women need to understand, she urged them to approach it with openness rather than fear. “So, for instance, AI is here. And let me tell you on my authority as a priest, AI is not a spiritual attack,” she added. Gomashie challenges women on values and mentorship Meanwhile, Minister for Tourism, Culture and Creative Arts Abla Dzifa Gomashie challenged women to reflect on the values, knowledge and principles they pass on to younger generations. She questioned whether the lessons being imparted to young people were appropriate for their development and whether the recipients were prepared to learn from them. “Teach a child the way they should grow. And when they grow, they will not depart from it. But what are we passing on now? And those we are passing the things on to, are they ready to receive it?” she asked. Drawing on the familiar analogy of leading a donkey to water without being able to force it to drink, the minister highlighted the limits of guidance when the person receiving it is unwilling to learn. Her remarks underscored the role of mentorship and personal responsibility in preparing younger generations to take up leadership positions. Women leaders share experiences The summit also featured contributions from former Electoral Commissioner Charlotte Osei, Administrator of the Ghana Medical Trust Fund Secretariat Obuobia Darko-Opoku, and Special Aide to President John Dramani Mahama Joyce Bawa Mogtari. The speakers shared experiences from their professional journeys and encouraged young women to develop their abilities, overcome barriers and take advantage of opportunities to contribute to national development. Founded by Ama Pratt, Press Secretary and Spokesperson to the Vice President, the summit was held under the theme, “Legacy and Leadership: Ghanaian Women Shaping the Past, Guiding the Future.” The event focused on sustaining the contributions of women in leadership while equipping younger generations with the knowledge, values and skills needed to carry that legacy forward.

items.title: La Bourse de Casablanca termine dans le vert
items.description: La Bourse de Casablanca a fini dans le vert mardi, son indice principal, le MASI, gagnant 0,52% à 17.041,91 points (pts). Le MASI 20, qui regroupe les 20 valeurs les plus liquides, a progressé de 0,15% à 1.229,78 pts et le MASI ESG, indice des entreprises ayant la meilleure notation ESG selon Moody's ESG Solutions, a pris 0,83% à 1.263,89 pts. De son côté, le MASI Mid and Small Cap, reflétant la performance des petites et moyennes entreprises cotées, a avancé de 0,78% à 1.631,45 pts. Sur le plan sectoriel, les indices « Participation et promotion immobilières » (+5,71%), « Chimie » (+3,91%) et « Ingénieries et biens d'équipement industriels » (+3,12%) ont signé les meilleures performances. À l'inverse, les secteurs « Sociétés de portefeuilles – Holdings » (-2,56%), « Transport » (-0,62%) et « Distributeurs » (-0,41%) ont affiché les plus fortes baisses. Les échanges ont atteint plus de 186 millions de dirhams (MDH), réalisés sur le marché central « Actions » et dominés par les transactions sur Attijariwafa bank (50,69 MDH), TGCC (38,53 MDH) et Sodep-Marsa Maroc (21,47 MDH). La capitalisation boursière s'est établie à plus de 1.004 milliards de dirhams. Aux valeurs individuelles, Addoha (+8,33% à 33,8 DH), Fenie Brossette (+7,31% à 337,5 DH), SNEP (+4,91% à 294,95 DH), T2S Group Holding (+4,45% à 209 DH) et Résidences Dar Saada (+4,39% à 161,8 DH) ont enregistré les plus fortes hausses. À l'opposé, les plus forts replis ont été accusés par Rebab Company (-4,54% à 98,9 DH), Delta Holding (-2,59% à 47 DH), Disway (-2,01% à 730 DH), Lesieur Cristal (-1,98% à 289,95 DH) et Maghreb Oxygène (-1,78% à 380 DH). items.title: Banfora : MÉDIATEUR SERVICES et ORANGE Burkina inaugurent officiellement une nouvelle boutique
items.description: Le jeudi 8 octobre 2026, la ville de Banfora a accueilli la cérémonie officielle d’ouverture de la boutique Orange Burkina, exploitée par MÉDIATEL SERVICES, en face du Centre hospitalier régional (CHR) de Banfora. L’événement a été marqué par plusieurs temps forts, notamment les allocutions des responsables, la remise de récompenses, la coupure symbolique du ruban, la visite des locaux, un repas partagé et des bénédictions. La cérémonie a réuni les responsables de la structure, des invités ainsi que des partenaires venus assister à cette ouverture officielle. Cette initiative s’inscrit dans une dynamique de rapprochement des services de télécommunication avec les populations de la cité du Paysan noir. La cérémonie a débuté par l’exécution de l’hymne national, suivie de plusieurs allocutions. À cette occasion, les responsables présents se sont exprimés sur l’importance de cette ouverture et les perspectives du partenariat entre MÉDIATEL SERVICES et Orange Burkina. Les différentes interventions ont constitué un moment privilégié pour présenter la vision du promoteur, Mahamadi Diendjeré, et souligner l’importance de la collaboration entre les différents acteurs. Elles ont également permis de mettre en lumière les attentes liées à l’implantation de cette boutique dans la ville de Banfora. Pour le promoteur, Mahamadi Diendjeré, l’objectif est de placer le client au cœur des préoccupations. « Mon client, mon boss. Dans cette boutique, presque tous les services de Orange Burkina seront mis à la disposition des clients et nous demandons à la population des TANNOUNYAN de s’approprier cette boutique pour son bon fonctionnement », a-t-il laissé entendre. Selon Cheick Oumar Diallo, chef du département de la région commerciale de l’Ouest, le choix de cet emplacement répond à la volonté de rapprocher les services d’Orange Burkina des populations de Banfora. Située en face du CHR, la boutique bénéficie d’un emplacement facilement identifiable par les habitants. « Nous souhaitons ainsi faciliter l’accès à nos services pour les clients de la région. Nous invitons également le personnel de cette boutique de prendre toutes les mesures pour bien accueillir les clients », a-t-il déclaré. Après les allocutions, les trois premiers clients de la boutique ont été récompensés. Ce geste a constitué l’un des temps forts de la cérémonie, apportant une touche particulière à cette ouverture officielle. La coupure du ruban a constitué l’un des moments les plus attendus de la cérémonie. Ce geste symbolique a consacré l’ouverture officielle de la boutique MÉDIATEL SERVICES, partenaire d’Orange Burkina à Banfora, et marqué le début de ses activités au service du public. À la suite de cette étape, les invités ont effectué une visite des locaux. Ils ont ainsi pu découvrir l’aménagement intérieur de la boutique ainsi que les différents espaces destinés à l’accueil et à la prise en charge de la clientèle. La cérémonie s’est poursuivie dans une atmosphère conviviale autour d’un repas partagé entre les responsables et les invités. Ce moment de fraternité a permis aux participants de prolonger les échanges dans un cadre détendu. Des bénédictions prononcées par les grands imams de Banfora ont également marqué la rencontre. Elles ont exprimé des vœux de réussite, de prospérité et de pérennité pour cette nouvelle boutique. Au terme de cette cérémonie inaugurale, les attentes portent désormais sur la qualité de l’accueil, la disponibilité des services et la satisfaction de la clientèle. Autant d’enjeux qui devront permettre à la boutique MÉDIATEL SERVICES, en partenariat avec Orange Burkina, de répondre aux besoins des populations de Banfora et de ses environs. L’article Banfora : MÉDIATEUR SERVICES et ORANGE Burkina inaugurent officiellement une nouvelle boutique est apparu en premier sur Faso7 .

GHS to distribute 80,000 pairs of locally-made protective footwear to health workers
items.description: The Ghana Health Service (GHS) will distribute 80,000 pairs of protective footwear to health professionals implementing the Free Primary Healthcare programme, following a donation by Sanford, World Shoe Ltd. and Samaritan’s Feet Ghana. The shoes are manufactured in Ghana using lightweight EVA foam and feature antimicrobial properties intended to help prevent infections. They are also designed to be biodegradable. Director-General of the Ghana Health Service, Dr Samuel Kaba Akoriyea, said the Service would work with its regional and district teams to ensure the shoes reach the intended beneficiaries. “We will communicate with our regional and district teams and support a process that is organised, transparent and consistent with the purpose of the donation,” he said. Vice President of Sanford World Clinic, Karoliina Slack, said the initiative was inspired by the sacrifices health workers make, often in facilities with limited equipment and infrastructure. “We wanted to give them a piece of something, a piece of hope, something that they will wear when they go to work, and they remember that across the ocean, in the US, there are lots of people that think of them and value them and understand the sacrifices that they make every day,” she said. Chairman and Chief Executive Officer of World Shoe and Samaritan’s Feet International, Manny Ohonme, said the donation demonstrates how locally manufactured products can address healthcare needs while creating jobs and supporting economic growth. “Our solution is not just about providing the shoes. So the shoes that you saw here today, 80,000, means people are employed,” he said. The organisations say they hope to build on the partnership to attract more stakeholders to support healthcare delivery and improve the well-being of health workers in Ghana.

items.title: Tebboune confie l’Intérieur à Brahim Merad, Saïd Sayoud garde les Transports
items.description: Brahim Merad retourne au ministère de l’Intérieur. Il a été nommé ce mardi 13 octobre à ce poste par le président de la République, Abdelmadjid Tebboune, en remplacement de Saïd Sayoud, a annoncé la Présidence dans un communiqué. Son prédécesseur qui était chargé de deux portefeuilles, l’Intérieur et les Transports, garde le deuxième où il retrouve aussi son poste initial. « Le Président de la République, M. Abdelmadjid Tebboune, a nommé aujourd'hui M. Brahim Merad ministre d'État, ministre de l'Intérieur et des Collectivités locales, et a désigné M. Saïd Sayoud ministre des Transports », a indiqué la Présidence de la République. Ministère de l’Intérieur : Brahim Merad retrouve son poste, Said Sayoud revient aux Transports M. Sayoud a été nommé en septembre 2025 à la tête d’un super ministère regroupant l’Intérieur, les Collectivités locales et les Transports. Il avait succédé à Brahim Merad à l’Intérieur au moment où il occupait depuis novembre 2024 le poste de ministre des Transports. Pour Brahim Merad, il a été nommé en septembre 2025 ministre d’État, chargé de l’inspection générale des services de l’État et des collectivités locales dans le gouvernement Sifi Ghrieb, après avoir dirigé le département de l’Intérieur pendant trois ans ( 9 septembre 2022 – 15 septembre 2025). Le changement à la tête du ministère de l’Intérieur survient quelques jours après les critiques formulées par le président de la République, Abdelmadjid Tebboune, à l’égard de Saïd Sayoud au sujet de la hausse des prix de la tomate. Il lui a notamment reproché d’avoir dit qu’en 60 ans, il n’a jamais vu la tomate atteindre le prix de 200 DA le kilo en août . items.title: Accusations d’usage de l’IA : Thélyson Orélien défend son roman
items.description: Le romancier Thélyson Orélien conteste les accusations selon lesquelles son livre C’était ça ou mourir aurait été écrit par une intelligence artificielle. Dans une déclaration intitulée « Ce roman que j’ai écrit », l’auteur revient sur la genèse de l’ouvrage, évoque son parcours personnel et reconnaît des erreurs de jeunesse, tout en dénonçant le harcèlement dont il affirme être victime. Son livre, qui a dépassé les 75 000 exemplaires vendus depuis la fin août, reste en lice pour le prix Renaudot. Thélyson Orélien a décidé de prendre la parole. Accusé d’avoir eu massivement recours à l’intelligence artificielle (IA) pour écrire C’était ça ou mourir, le romancier défend l’authenticité de son travail et revendique pleinement la paternité de son livre. « C’est une calomnie et une hérésie », affirme-t-il dans son communiqué transmis à l’Agence France-Presse (AFP) par son éditeur français, Grasset. Intitulé « Ce roman que j’ai écrit », le texte constitue une réponse aux critiques apparues depuis le 21 septembre, date à partir de laquelle, selon l’auteur, les accusations se sont multipliées. « Un écrivain parle par ses écrits et ses écrits parlent pour lui. Mais le silence a son prix : à force de me taire, je laissais les autres raconter mon histoire à ma place », explique-t-il pour justifier sa prise de parole. Un roman né en 2017 Pour étayer sa défense, Thélyson Orélien revient sur les origines de C’était ça ou mourir. Il affirme avoir commencé à écrire le livre à l’automne 2017, à Laval, au Québec, avant d’en achever une première version en 2019. Ce premier manuscrit comptait plus de 300 pages. L’écriture s’est ensuite poursuivie à travers plusieurs phases de révision. L’auteur dit avoir supprimé des scènes, retravaillé des passages, déplacé des éléments du récit et modifié certains personnages avant la publication de l’ouvrage en 2026. Il insiste notamment sur l’ancienneté de son personnage principal, Jonas Dorléon, ainsi que sur la place occupée par Haïti, le Québec, la migration et l’exil dans le récit. Des thèmes qu’il rattache à son propre parcours et aux histoires recueillies au fil des années. « Haïti, la mère biologique, habite ce roman depuis le premier jour, tout comme le Québec adoptif, la migration, l’exil : des histoires que j’ai moi-même vécues et d’autres que j’ai entendues au fil des années », écrit-il. L’écrivain reconnaît avoir utilisé certains outils pour effectuer des recherches, notamment sur des expressions étrangères. Il réfute toutefois toute intervention de l’intelligence artificielle dans la rédaction du texte. « Aucune phrase de ce livre n’a été créée par une machine, pas plus que le sens ou l’ordonnance d’un récit qui vient de mes tripes », assure-t-il. Un succès commercial sur fond de controverse La polémique intervient alors que C’était ça ou mourir connaît un succès commercial important. Selon les informations communiquées, le roman a dépassé les 75 000 exemplaires vendus depuis la fin août. L’ouvrage est également toujours en lice pour le prix Renaudot, l’une des distinctions littéraires les plus suivies de la rentrée française. Ce succès contribue à placer le livre au centre de l’attention, tandis que les interrogations sur les conditions de son écriture alimentent le débat. Thélyson Orélien rejette les accusations d’utilisation massive de l’IA et demande que son travail soit apprécié à partir du texte lui-même. « Ce que je demande tient désormais en une phrase : qu’on juge le roman C’était ça ou mourir pour ce qu’il est », déclare-t-il. L’auteur ne réclame toutefois pas que les interrogations sur son passé soient écartées. Il estime plutôt qu’elles ne doivent pas être confondues avec la question de l’origine de son roman, dont il situe le début de l’écriture en 2017. Des erreurs de jeunesse reconnues Dans son communiqué, Thélyson Orélien revient également sur des écrits antérieurs et sur des erreurs qu’il reconnaît avoir commises dans sa jeunesse. Il rappelle avoir quitté Haïti en 2010, après le séisme dévastateur, en passant par la République dominicaine, un parcours qui présente des similitudes avec celui de son personnage, Jonas Dorléon. À l’époque, explique-t-il, il lisait beaucoup et cherchait à découvrir les univers de nombreux écrivains. Il cite notamment René Depestre, Édouard Glissant, Aimé Césaire, Patrick Chamoiseau, Jacques Stephen Alexis, René Char, Charles Péguy, Ernest Hemingway, Gabriel García Márquez et Fiodor Dostoïevski. Il évoque aussi l’influence que certaines lectures ont pu exercer sur lui, notamment Le Matin des magiciens, de Louis Pauwels et Jacques Bergier. Mais il distingue clairement l’admiration littéraire de l’appropriation de textes. « J’ai commis des erreurs inacceptables, malgré la jeunesse et l’inexpérience. Je le regrette profondément et présente mes excuses sans réserve », reconnaît-il. Cette reconnaissance constitue un volet important de sa déclaration. L’auteur ne cherche pas à nier son passé, mais conteste que celui-ci puisse suffire à établir que son roman aurait été produit par une intelligence artificielle. « Une erreur de jeunesse ne peut tenir lieu de preuve contre un roman débuté en 2017 et qui sera finalement publié en 2026 », soutient-il. La critique, oui, le harcèlement, non Au-delà de la controverse littéraire, Thélyson Orélien dénonce les conséquences personnelles des accusations portées contre lui. Il estime que la remise en cause de son travail a fini par toucher à son identité et à son humanité. « En attribuant à une machine un texte qui est mien, qui est celui de tous les miens, on n’est pas seulement venu contester ma qualité d’écrivain mais mon humanité », écrit-il. Il affirme également subir des menaces, du harcèlement raciste et ce qu’il décrit comme un lynchage médiatique depuis plusieurs semaines. L’écrivain reconnaît néanmoins le droit des journalistes à enquêter et celui des lecteurs à examiner ses anciennes publications. Il admet aussi que son roman puisse être critiqué, voire rejeté par certains lecteurs. « La critique est toujours légitime, mais les menaces, le lynchage médiatique et le harcèlement raciste que je subis depuis des semaines sont insoutenables », déplore-t-il. Un appel à lire le roman pour ce qu’il raconte En conclusion, Thélyson Orélien revient à l’essentiel : l’histoire qu’il dit avoir voulu raconter à travers Jonas Dorléon et les blessures liées à la migration et à l’exil. Il présente C’était ça ou mourir comme le fruit d’un travail personnel, nourri par son expérience et celle d’autres migrants. Son ambition, assure-t-il, n’était ni de gagner des prix ni de devenir célèbre, mais de faire entendre une histoire susceptible de toucher les lecteurs au-delà de leurs origines. « Je n’ai pas écrit ce livre pour gagner des prix ou devenir célèbre. Je n’ai rien à prouver aux gens qui m’accusent », affirme-t-il. Alors que le roman poursuit son parcours commercial et reste en lice pour le prix Renaudot, la déclaration de l’auteur expose sa ligne de défense : reconnaître ses erreurs passées, réfuter les accusations relatives à l’intelligence artificielle et demander que son œuvre soit jugée sur son contenu. À ce stade, le communiqué restitue la position de Thélyson Orélien. Les accusations relatives à l’utilisation de l’IA, comme les arguments avancés pour les contester, doivent être distingués des faits établis par une vérification indépendante. C.G. DIOP

items.title: Bas-Mono : Des chefs traditionnels et des leaders religieux sensibilisés à la promotion de nouvelles normes sociales
items.description: Afagnan, 13 oct. (ATOP) – Des chefs traditionnels, des leaders religieux et des jeunes en milieu extrascolaire de la préfecture de Bas-Mono ont été sensibilisés à leur rôle dans la promotion de nouvelles normes sociales favorables à la protection des droits des femmes et des filles du 7 au 10 octobre à Afagnan. L’activité est initiée par l’ONG La Colombe dans le cadre du projet « Améliorer les droits et la santé sexuelle et reproductive et santé maternelle, néonatale, infantile et des adolescents et la nutrition en Afrique de l’Ouest et du Centre ». Elle a bénéficié de l’appui technique et financier d’ONU Femmes, à travers le Fonds Muskoka. Les travaux ont permis de renforcer les connaissances des participants sur les normes sociales, leur influence sur les comportements individuels et collectifs, ainsi que les pratiques à promouvoir, à abandonner ou à transformer pour favoriser l’égalité de genre, la protection et la cohésion sociale. Les jeunes extrascolaires Les chefs traditionnels ont été entretenus sur les différences entre normes sociales, traditions et pratiques culturelles, ainsi que sur l’organisation de séances d’information dans leurs communautés. Les leaders religieux ont, pour leur part, été instruits sur les droits des femmes et des filles, les violences basées sur le genre, leurs causes et conséquences, les mécanismes de référence, la santé sexuelle et reproductive des jeunes, la santé maternelle et infantile ainsi que les bonnes pratiques nutritionnelles. Les jeunes ont quant à eux été sensibilisés aux infections sexuellement transmissibles, aux violences sexuelles, aux comportements à risque et à leurs conséquences, ainsi qu’à l’estime et à la confiance en soi. Le préfet de Bas-Mono, Sogbo Kokou Amétépé, a félicité l’ONG pour son engagement en faveur de l’épanouissement des femmes. Il a exhorté les bénéficiaires à faire tache d’huile des enseignements reçus dans leurs communautés. La coordonnatrice de l’ONG La Colombe, Mme Akakpo Adjoa, a souligné le rôle déterminant des chefs traditionnels et des leaders religieux dans l’évolution des normes sociales. ATOP/DK/MG

items.title: Un homme interpellé après le décès présumé d’une patiente à la suite d’une intervention chirurgicale
items.description: Présenté sous le surnom de «docteur» Tanoh et comme un spécialiste du Brazilian Butt Lift (BBL), un homme a été interpellé par la Police économique ivoirienne dans une affaire liée au décès d’une patiente après une intervention esthétique. Selon la Police Secours, qui a rapporté les faits, le lundi 12 octobre 2026, le mis en cause aurait pris la fuite avant d’être retrouvé par les enquêteurs. L’affaire soulève des interrogations sur les conditions de réalisation de certaines interventions esthétiques à Abidjan. D’après les informations publiées, le lundi 12 octobre 2026, par Police Secours, l’homme connu sous le nom de «docteur» Tanoh est mis en cause dans une affaire concernant le décès d’une patiente à la suite d’un Brazilian Butt Lift (BBL), une intervention chirurgicale visant notamment à augmenter le volume des fesses. Après le drame présumé, il aurait pris la fuite avant d’être retrouvé et interpellé par les éléments de la section Commerce et Contrefaçon de la Police économique. Les circonstances exactes du décès et les conditions dans lesquelles l’intervention a été pratiquée n’ont, à ce stade, pas été précisées. Les circonstances du décès à éclaircir L’enquête devra notamment déterminer les conditions de réalisation de l’intervention, vérifier les qualifications professionnelles du mis en cause et établir les éventuelles responsabilités dans cette affaire. Le surnom de « docteur » qui lui est attribué ne permet pas, à lui seul, de conclure qu’il possède les qualifications requises pour pratiquer des actes médicaux. Le Brazilian Butt Lift est une intervention esthétique qui comporte des risques et nécessite des compétences médicales adaptées, un environnement approprié ainsi qu’un suivi rigoureux. La vérification des qualifications du praticien et des conditions de prise en charge constitue donc un enjeu essentiel pour la sécurité des patientes. En l’état des informations disponibles, les circonstances du décès restent à établir. Le mis en cause bénéficie de la présomption d’innocence jusqu’à ce que sa culpabilité soit légalement démontrée. D’éventuelles victimes invitées à se manifester Par ailleurs, les personnes qui estiment avoir été victimes des agissements du dénommé Tanoh sont invitées à se rapprocher de la section Commerce et Contrefaçon de la Police économique, située au Plateau, à Abidjan, afin de signaler les faits et, si nécessaire, de déposer plainte. Ces éventuels témoignages pourraient contribuer à éclairer les enquêteurs sur les pratiques du mis en cause et sur l’existence d’autres faits susceptibles d’être examinés. L’enjeu est désormais de faire toute la lumière sur ce décès, d’établir les circonstances de l’intervention et de déterminer les éventuelles responsabilités, sans préjuger de l’issue de l’enquête. Par Valentin SOMANDE L’article Un homme interpellé après le décès présumé d’une patiente à la suite d’une intervention chirurgicale est apparu en premier sur Wakat Séra .

items.title: PM Shehbaz takes allies into confidence on KP governor's rule, says Centre made every effort to avoid 'extreme step'
items.description: ISLAMABAD: Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif on Tuesday took the allies of the ruling PML-N into confidence on the imposition of governor’s rule in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, saying that the Centre made every effort to avoid this “extreme step”. The Centre on Sunday imposed governor’s rule in KP and emergency in 12 of its districts, citing the provincial government’s “deliberate disengagement” from the fight against terrorism. PM Shehbaz held a meeting with leaders of the Muttahida Qaumi Movement-Pakistan (MQM-P), as well as a separate huddle with a parliamentary delegation comprising representatives of PML-Q, Balochistan Awami Party (BAP), Istehkam-i-Pakistan Party (IPP) and PML-Zia. During the meeting with the MQM-P delegation led by Education Minister Khalid Maqbool Siddiqui, the two sides exchanged views on the country’s overall and political situation, the PM Office (PMO) said. The prime minister said the government had to take this “most difficult decision” in the interest of the people of KP. “We made every effort to avoid taking this extreme step in any way. We engaged in negotiations with an open heart, but did not receive a positive response from the other side,” he was quoted as saying. The premier noted that rising terrorist attacks in KP were targeting ordinary citizens and security forces, while the provincial government “failed to openly raise its voice against terrorist groups”. PM Shehbaz also termed the PTI’s long march a “conspiracy to destroy the country’s improving economy”. According to PMO, the MQM-P delegation assured the prime minister of its full support for the government’s decisions regarding KP. On the MQM’s side, the delegation included Health Minister Mustafa Kamal, Senator Amir Waliuddin Chishti, Senator Khalida Ateeb, MNA Farooq Sattar, Syed Waseem Hussain, Aasia Ishaque Siddiqui, Javed Hanif Khan, Muhammad Moeen Aamir Pirzada, Muhammad Iqbal Khan, Hassan Sabir, Sadiq Iftikhar, Arshad Abdullah Vohra, Syed Hafizuddin, Syed Aminul Haque, Khawaja Azharul Hassan, Ahmad Saleem Siddiqui, Farhan Chishti, Nighat Shakeel Khan, Sabheen Ghoury, Rana Ansar, Sofia Saeed Shah, and Sanjay Perwani. In the second meeting with other parties, PM Shehbaz explained the reasons behind the federal government’s decision to take constitutional measures, state-run APP reported. He said the conduct of the PTI-led KP government in the province and its failure to adopt an unequivocal stance against terrorism had posed risks to Pakistan’s growing economy. The premier highlighted that the federal government had provided more than Rs800 billion to KP under the National Finance Commission (NFC) arrangements to support efforts against terrorism. However, he said, the provincial government had failed to take effective measures to strengthen the capacity of its Counter-Terrorism Department (CTD) and establish Safe City projects to improve its counterterrorism capabilities. According to the PM’s Office, the parliamentary delegation expressed its support for the federal government amid the prevailing situation and appreciated the prime minister’s leadership during what it described as difficult circumstances. The delegation also said the people of KP had remained deprived of adequate development in health, education and infrastructure during the PTI’s tenure in the province. It expressed confidence that, with the federal government’s cooperation, development and prosperity in KP would advance in line with other parts of the country. The delegation included BAP President and Science and Technology Minister Khalid Magsi; former Senate chairman Sadiq Sanjrani of BAP, senators Manzoor Kakar, Abdul Qadir Baloch, Dinesh Kumar and Samina Mumtaz Zehri; PML-Q President and Human Resource Development Minister Chaudhry Salik Hussain; and representatives of the IPP and PML-Zia. From the government, Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar, Defence Minister Khawaja Asif, Law Minister Azam Nazeer Tarar, Parliamentary Affairs Minister Dr Tariq Fazal Chaudhry and PM’s Adviser on Political Affairs Rana Sanaullah attended both meetings. ‘What other path did we have?’ Later, he addressed a parliamentary meeting of his PML-N and said, “When terrorism is spreading, sacrifices are being made day and night, and this party (PTI) is exhausting all its resources and time round the clock to create instability.” The premier emphasised that the people of KP had been wanting “projects of development and prosperity for the past 13 years”, such as schools, universities, hospitals, better law and order, and an end to corruption. However, he contended, there was “not zero, but negative attention” towards these matters, and “all attention and resources” were instead diverted towards long marches and protests. “Can any respectable society tolerate this? Even the question does not arise. So what other path did we have?” he asked, quipping if the Centre should have remained as “silent spectators”. The prime minister noted that the Centre was “compelled to make this decision” after the Oct 3 talks between the government and the opposition collapsed . Elaborating on the dialogue process, PM Shehbaz said, “There was a moment when it was set in stone that an agreement was about to be reached, all demands were settled.” He added that a consensus-based draft was ready, but the PTI team sought some more time to consult Sohail Afridi — the KP chief minister whose role now stands non-functional. “The rest is history. […] They were ordered that you have to create another May 9, even go beyond it and wreak havoc; you must not accept anything,” the premier added. He went on to recall his engagement with Jamiat Ulemai-i-Islam–Fazl (JUI-F) chief Maulana Fazlur Rehman to reduce tensions , which was followed by the Oct 11 cabinet meeting. “After all consultations and arguments, it was decided that this is the moment to save Pakistan. We must not wait any further, else everything will be set on fire and we will be left with regret.” PM Shehbaz reiterated, “We were compelled to make the decision of imposing emergency. This is no other choice because Pakistan is first.” He expressed his hope that the newly appointed KP Advisory Council , which will work under the governor, would work to improve the living conditions and safety in the province. The prime minister asserted that terrorism had been eradicated in most parts of the country several years ago, but had resurged recently. He lamented that law enforcers were being martyred daily in KP and Balochistan. “If this bloodshed is not brought to an end like it was in 2018, then the journey of development made in the past 2.5 years… this journey is continuing gradually.” “If one provincial government is not only determined to end that journey […] but that party is determined on destruction and comes to thinking that if they make progress, what will be our value; how regrettable it is.” The prime minister recalled the November 2024 protest by the PTI in Islamabad, as well as its 2014 rallies at the federal capital’s D-Chowk. “When someone is bent on ending the country’s progress, they are engaged in sit-ins, verbal abuse and allegations, instead of standing with the Centre and the armed forces and empowering the police and CTD,” he said. PM Shehbaz said even an enemy would not make the remarks made by Afridi in recent weeks. He criticised the PTI leader for not expressing sympathies with the martyrs’ families and for “not willing to say a single word” against terrorists. At the outset of his address, the premier highlighted his government’s efforts to cooperate with the PTI-led governments in KP. He recalled his meeting with former KP chief minister Ali Amin Gandapur , saying, “We told him in every way that we will cooperate with them … combatting terrorism is our shared responsibility.” He noted that he had also met with Sohail Afridi — whose role as the KP CM is currently non-functional due to governor’s rule — and asserted that the Centre tried its best to work with the KP government. At one point, the premier said International Monetary Fund (IMF) Managing Director Kristalina Georgieva recently told him, “This is a new Pakistan”, as she praised the country’s economic reforms. He recalled his meetings last month with international financial institutions and stressed that praise from such independent firms for Pakistan “restored” his faith in the country’s progress.

items.title: GoldBod boosts local jobs as 90% of gold undergoes refining in Ghana – Sammy Gyamfi
items.description: The Ghana Gold Board (GoldBod) is strengthening local value addition in the gold sector, with between 80 and 90 per cent of the gold it purchases and exports now refined in Ghana, its Chief Executive Officer, Sammy Gyamfi, has disclosed. He said the development was helping to create employment opportunities, retain revenue within the domestic economy and support the growth of local industries. Speaking before Parliament’s Public Accounts Committee on Tuesday, October 13, Mr Gyamfi said the shift towards local refining represented a significant departure from previous practices, under which much of the country’s gold was exported without being refined locally. He explained that the increased use of domestic refineries was helping Ghana capture more economic benefits from its mineral resources instead of allowing such opportunities to be realised in foreign destinations. “I’m happy to report to this honourable committee that, as we speak, about 80 to 90 per cent of the gold we purchase and export is refined here locally,” he said. According to him, the refineries operate around the clock and employ Ghanaians, particularly young people, while ensuring that refining fees that would otherwise be paid abroad remain in the country. Mr Gyamfi added that the benefits extended beyond gold refining, as silver recovered during the process was also being retained locally to generate foreign exchange and provide raw materials for Ghana’s fabrication industry. He said the approach was helping to strengthen domestic industrial activity, create jobs and increase the economic returns from the country’s gold resources, while advancing GoldBod’s broader mandate of supporting foreign exchange generation and the regulation of Ghana’s gold trading sector.

items.title: The search for the politically unblemished: Are we asking the impossible of public appointees?
items.description: The controversy surrounding President John Dramani Mahama’s appointment of Emelia Afi Agbenyo as a Deputy Chairperson of Ghana’s Electoral Commission (EC) raises a question that deserves serious national reflection. How do we determine whether a person appointed to a sensitive public office can be trusted to discharge the responsibilities of that office fairly, independently and without political interference? The question is important because the credibility of our elections depends, in part, on public confidence in those entrusted with managing them. On 12 October 2026, President Mahama swore in Emelia Afi Agbenyo and Dr Joseph Kwaku Asamoah as Deputy Chairpersons of the Electoral Commission, urging them to perform their duties without favour towards any political party, candidate or government. The appointments have prompted renewed political debate about impartiality and the selection of persons for positions of national importance. Source: Ghana News Agency, 12 October 2026. Mindset Transformation Initiative (MTI) believes this debate presents an opportunity to look beyond the immediate political contest and examine a more fundamental issue: Are we placing so much emphasis on finding individuals without perceived political associations that we risk neglecting the stronger safeguards needed to protect our public institutions? The Difficult Search for a Politically Unblemished Person In a politically divided society, the demand for neutral and impartial public officers is understandable. Citizens want judges who dispense justice without political considerations, electoral commissioners who administer elections without favour, and public officials who serve the Republic rather than the interests of the government that appointed them. These are reasonable expectations. However, we must also confront a practical difficulty. In a society where political parties influence public discourse, professional networks, civic participation and national debate, how easy is it to identify a competent individual who has never held a political opinion, associated with a politically active person, supported a public policy or been perceived as sympathetic to one political tradition? The expression politically unblemished can become an elusive standard if it means that an appointee must have no past association, opinion, or circumstance that a political opponent might question. A person may have a political history and still possess the integrity to serve impartially. Another may have no known political affiliation yet lack the courage to resist pressure, the discipline to follow the law or the moral strength to act against the interests of those who appointed them. Political neutrality cannot therefore be established solely by examining a person’s background. It must also be demonstrated through conduct, decisions and a willingness to uphold the law, even when doing so displeases powerful interests. This does not mean that a candidate’s political history should be ignored. Relevant associations, conflicts of interest and evidence of partisan conduct deserve careful scrutiny. It means that such scrutiny should be based on credible evidence and fair standards rather than political suspicion alone. Consistency Matters, but So Does Institutional Integrity MTI recognises the concerns being raised by political parties about consistency in public appointments. Where one party demands strict standards of neutrality while in opposition but applies a different standard when in government, public confidence suffers. Political parties must be prepared to defend the same principles regardless of which party holds power. If a party believes that an electoral commissioner should not have a close and demonstrable relationship with a political organisation, that principle should apply whether the appointment is made by an NDC or NPP administration. If a party argues that appointments to the judiciary must be protected from political influence, it should support the same protections when its political interests are not directly affected. The test of a principle is whether its supporters are prepared to uphold it when doing so is inconvenient. Nevertheless, political consistency alone will not guarantee institutional independence. Even where an appointment process is transparent, and the appointee has an impressive professional record, the institution must still have systems that prevent improper interference and make misconduct difficult to conceal. The central question must therefore extend beyond who has been appointed to include the conditions under which that person will exercise authority. Institutions Must Be Stronger Than the Individuals Who Lead Them Ghana’s Electoral Commission is a constitutional institution with a responsibility that extends beyond the interests of any government or political party. Article 46 of the 1992 Constitution provides that, in performing its functions, the Commission shall not be subject to the control or direction of any person or authority, except as provided by the Constitution or other applicable law. This principle is fundamental. The Commission must serve the Republic and its citizens. Yet constitutional independence must be supported by practical arrangements that protect the electoral process from manipulation, undue pressure, administrative abuse and individual misconduct. No democratic country should have to depend entirely on the personal virtue of the people appointed to administer its elections. Good people can make mistakes. People can face pressure. People can change their positions. Institutions must be designed to withstand these human realities. The same principle applies to the judiciary. We need judges of integrity, but we also need transparent judicial processes, clear rules of professional conduct, independent disciplinary procedures and decisions that can be examined against the law and the evidence. The objective should be to create institutions in which the rules are stronger than personal loyalties, and accountability is more powerful than political influence. What Would Stronger Electoral Safeguards Look Like? MTI proposes that Ghana’s national conversation should give greater attention to the practical safeguards that protect the integrity of elections, irrespective of who occupies the leadership of the Electoral Commission. First, strengthen the transparency of electoral procedures The processes for voter registration, collation, transmission, verification and declaration of results must be governed by clear, publicly available rules. Any changes to those procedures should be properly explained, legally authorised and communicated in good time Second, establish effective independent verification Election results should be supported by verifiable records at each stage of the process. Party agents, accredited observers and other legally authorised stakeholders should have meaningful opportunities to observe procedures, obtain the records they are entitled to receive and raise objections through established channels. Where electronic systems are used, they should be supported by appropriate security controls, independent technical audits and reliable contingency arrangements. Third, strengthen accountability for electoral misconduct There should be clear procedures for investigating credible allegations of interference, falsification, deliberate obstruction or abuse of electoral authority. Investigations must be impartial, timely and subject to the law. Proven misconduct should attract appropriate sanctions, regardless of the rank or political connections of the person involved. Fourth, protect the independence of election officials at every level Electoral integrity cannot rest on the character of the Chairperson and Deputy Chairpersons alone. Regional and district officials, returning officers, collation teams and other personnel must work under professional standards that protect them from improper political pressure. Their duties, reporting lines and disciplinary arrangements should be clearly defined. Fifth, make electoral processes more open to public scrutiny Public confidence grows when citizens can understand how results are produced and how disputes are resolved. Clear documentation, timely publication of legally releasable results, transparent reconciliation procedures and accessible complaint mechanisms can help reduce suspicion and strengthen trust. Sixth, improve the appointment process itself The selection of persons for sensitive constitutional offices should be transparent, merit-based and supported by credible scrutiny of professional competence, integrity, independence and potential conflicts of interest. The public should be able to understand the criteria applied and the reasons candidates are considered suitable. The Constitution Review Committee’s December 2025 recommendations on Electoral Commission appointments provide a useful starting point for examining reforms, including open competitive recruitment, a more structured selection process and parliamentary approval of nominees. These recommendations should be considered on their merits as part of the wider national reform debate. The purpose of these safeguards is straightforward: to make electoral manipulation difficult, detectable and punishable, whoever might attempt it Should We Abandon the Search for Neutrality? MTI does not suggest that impartiality is unimportant or that political history should be irrelevant to public appointments. Nor should we lower the standards expected of people entrusted with sensitive constitutional responsibilities. Rather, we must distinguish between demanding impartial conduct and expecting to find a person whom nobody can accuse of political sympathy. The first is a necessary democratic standard. The second may become an endless political exercise, particularly when rival parties judge the same individual according to their competing interests. Perhaps, therefore, Ghana should reconsider the weight it places on searching for a supposedly politically spotless candidate. We should retain rigorous scrutiny of an appointee’s record, but direct more of our national energy towards building systems that ensure that no appointee can easily compromise the institution they serve. This is particularly important because public appointments are made within a constitutional and political framework. The fact that an officeholder was appointed by a President does not, by itself, establish that the individual will act in the President’s interest. Equally, the absence of a known party affiliation does not automatically establish impartiality. The fair approach is to examine the appointment process, the candidate’s qualifications and record, any credible evidence of conflicts or partisan conduct, and the safeguards that will govern the exercise of the office. In the case of the Electoral Commission, the ultimate test should be whether the electoral system can produce credible, verifiable and legally defensible results, irrespective of the political identity of the people managing it. A Call for a Change in National Mindset As a civic organisation committed to responsibility, integrity, discipline and national development, Mindset Transformation Initiative believes that Ghana’s democratic maturity requires a shift in how we approach these matters. We must move from a political culture that concentrates almost exclusively on the perceived loyalties of individuals to one that demands competence, accountability and institutional resilience. Political parties have a legitimate responsibility to scrutinise appointments. Civil society has a duty to ask difficult questions. The media must investigate and report responsibly. Citizens must insist on transparency. Appointees must understand that public office is a trust held on behalf of the Republic. All these responsibilities are complementary. We must also resist the temptation to pronounce individuals guilty of political bias without credible evidence. Public confidence is not strengthened when allegations are treated as established facts simply because they suit a political argument. Equally, allegations should not be dismissed merely because they concern an appointee of the governing party. The same standards must apply to everyone. A mature democracy should be able to scrutinise an appointment firmly while respecting the appointee’s right to be assessed fairly. It should also be able to demand stronger institutional safeguards without making assumptions about the intentions of any particular officeholder. Conclusion: Let Us Protect the Sanctity of the Vote Mindset Transformation Initiative appreciates the concerns being expressed by political parties about consistency, impartiality and public confidence in appointments to the Electoral Commission. These concerns deserve a fair hearing, and the appointment process must always be open to legitimate scrutiny. However, we believe Ghana must look beyond the search for a person who is perceived to have no political blemish. That search can become subjective, politically selective and difficult to conclude. Perhaps it is time to place less emphasis on the impossible expectation of finding a politically unblemished individual and greater emphasis on creating an electoral system that no individual can easily manipulate. We should insist on qualified, ethical and impartial public officers. At the same time, we must establish safeguards that make interference difficult, ensure that irregularities can be detected, provide effective remedies for disputes and hold offenders accountable under the law. The sanctity of the vote must never depend solely on the goodwill of the person occupying an office. It must be protected by sound laws, transparent procedures, independent verification, professional electoral administration and effective accountability. Whether the Electoral Commission is led by persons appointed under an NDC, NPP or any future administration, the same safeguards must apply. No political party should have to trust the personal goodwill of its opponent to believe that an election has been conducted fairly. Our national objective should be to build an electoral system in which the results reflect the will of the Ghanaian people, where that will can be independently verified, and where no amount of attempted manipulation can overturn the lawful outcome without detection and appropriate remedy. The ultimate safeguard for Ghana’s democracy is not merely the hope that we appoint the right people. It is the determination to build institutions that compel every person, regardless of political affiliation or personal interest, to do what is right under the law. That is the mindset Ghana must cultivate. ******* By Sidney Justin Tehoda

items.title: Why Home Advantage Matters in Football, Tennis and Basketball
items.description: Home advantage is one of the most widely accepted beliefs in modern athletics. It is the idea that teams often perform better in front of their fans. However, this does not mean that the home team will always win in reality. Anything can happen in football, tennis, and basketball, and the win can go either way irrespective of how hostile the condition is. Although the general home-field advantage is worth considering, it’s just that it works quite differently for each sport. In team sports like football and basketball, the collective roar of thousands of fans can instantly shift momentum or even influence the referee’s decisions. So, don’t be surprised when the odds change drastically in the blink of an eye when betting on live matches at 1xBet Ghana , to reflect the match’s current momentum. Bettors should pay close attention to the smallest details that can contribute to the match’s outcome. How Home Advantage Works in Sports Home advantage is the belief that athletes and sports teams win more often and perform better at home than when they travel to face an opponent. In team sports, this usually means playing in front of the club’s own supporters. In tennis, it can mean playing in a player’s home country or at a tournament where they are comfortable with the conditions. Below are some factors that contribute to home advantage in sport: Support from home crowds: A roaring stadium has a massive psychological impact on the players. The noise triggers an adrenaline rush, which helps home players fight through exhaustion during the dying minutes. A loud crowd can also make communication harder for the visiting team and add pressure during important moments. Reduced travel demands: Traveling is stressful and can affect sleeping patterns, diets, and overall concentration. Home teams don’t experience these disruptions, giving them an edge. Familiar playing surfaces and conditions: Home teams already understand their own training grounds and stadium layout. This makes it easier for them to easily execute tactics and play to instruction. The demand to impress the fans: The natural instinct to give the fans bragging rights can bring a major mental boost during the game. Players naturally play with more aggression and confidence when playing in front of their fans. Note that home advantage is not all it takes to win a match. A team with poor form can still lose at home. A strong away team can also perform well in hostile conditions. Football vs Tennis vs Basketball: Which Has the Strongest Home Advantage? Home advantage doesn’t work the same way across these three sports. For instance, Chelsea were unbeaten at home for 86 consecutive Premier League games from 2004 to 2008. During that time, they won multiple League titles, domestic cups, and played in several Champions League knockout matches. Moreover, a tennis player may perform better at a certain tennis surface or tournament than another. For example, Rafael Nadal has a 90.5% career win percentage on clay, losing just 51 times and winning 484 games on the surface. Another notable home record win in the NBA is held by San Antonio Spurs in the 2015/16 season. The Spurs did 40-1 at home, and the single loss didn’t happen until game 39 of the home schedule. So, it is difficult to conclude that a particular sport has the strongest home advantage over the other. Fans should instead focus on the entertainment that each sport has to offer. Why Home Advantage Changes from Match to Match Home advantage is only one of the things that can play a part in the outcome of a match. There are other contributing factors to consider. For instance, the quality of the competing teams can play a crucial role in how the game outcome will be. A bottom-tier football or basketball team will rarely beat a championship team simply because they are playing at home. In the same way, a major football match in a famous stadium can create a different environment from a low-profile league game. Therefore, the importance of the game, the health of the roster, and the distance the visitors had to travel can also influence the match. In tournament formats, a massive cross-country road trip can drastically affect a team’s physical freshness compared to short, regular travel. How Home Advantage Can Influence Football, Tennis and Basketball Betting Home advantage is one metric gamblers should consider when forecasting sports betting selections. It is advisable to use home advantage as part of a wider analysis of sports bet , but it should not be treated as a guaranteed way to predict results. In football, the most familiar market is the home win, draw or away win. A team’s home record can make it easier to forecast the possibility of getting any of these three outcomes. For example, a team that performs well at home may have an advantage over an opponent that struggles on the road. However, recent form, injuries, squad quality and the strength of the opposition still need to be considered. A strong home record alone does not mean a home win is the best choice. In basketball, home advantage can be considered in both the moneyline and point spread markets. The moneyline focuses on which team wins the game, while the point spread gives the stronger team a points handicap. A home team may be more likely to win, but the spread can still make the matchup less straightforward if the visiting team is expected to keep the game close. Tennis has its own set of betting options. The match-winner market is the most direct option, while set markets focus on how the match may develop. A player’s home advantage may come from crowd support, knowledge of the court and local playing conditions. But surface form can be more important than simply playing in front of a home crowd. Other Factors to Consider Beyond Home Advantage Home advantage should also be used carefully when analyzing the outcome of a match. A team’s old home record may include different players, coaches and opponents. A tennis player’s results from several years ago may say little about current form. The same applies to basketball teams after major roster changes. The best approach is to treat home advantage as one piece of information, since it doesn’t reveal the full picture. The table below reveals the different factors that can affect football, tennis and basketball performances and results. Factor Football Tennis Basketball Crowd influence High Moderate High Travel demands High Moderate to High High Familiar playing conditions Moderate High High Team communication High Not really High Pressure from home fans High High High Venue familiarity Moderate High High Home Advantage in the Modern Professional Sport Era In modern professional sports, there is growing evidence that the traditional weight of home advantage is gradually shrinking. Professional athletes have better travel arrangements, training facilities and recovery methods than in the past. Teams also use data to prepare for different opponents and playing environments. Players are now more accustomed to international travel. Many compete in different countries throughout the year, so unfamiliar surroundings may not be as difficult as they once were. While the physical gap between hosting and traveling is narrower today than it has ever been in sports history, Supporters still create noise. As such, the emotional spark of a passionate home crowd and the baseline comfort of local conditions will always matter. When Home Advantage Matters Less in Sports Home advantage doesn’t sometimes count in some matches. However, that doesn’t take away the game’s intensity and competitiveness. It’s just that playing at home doesn’t matter as much. Below are some conditions where the home advantage matters less: Neutral venues: When neither side plays in its usual stadium, both teams have to adapt to an unfamiliar environment. The crowd may also be split between the two sides. Low attendance: If there are few supporters, the home team may receive less of the energy normally associated with playing at home. Players’ experience: Elite teams and athletes travel regularly and have professional support staff who help them manage their wellbeing. This can reduce some of the problems associated with playing away from home. Opponent’s strength: A very strong team may be able to control a match despite playing away. In the same way, a weak home side does not automatically become a strong team because it is playing in familiar surroundings. Conclusion The venue in which a match will be played can dictate the atmosphere of the game. As such, home advantage can bring confidence, concentration, energy, and preparation to players. Football teams can benefit from their stadium, supporters and familiarity with the pitch. Basketball teams can use crowd energy and court familiarity to their advantage. Tennis players can gain from local support, familiar surfaces and reduced travel. However, none of these factors guarantees success. The better football team can still win away from home and the better tennis player can also win even when the surface conditions are not favorable. In the end, an outstanding performance will overcome any disadvantage caused by not playing at home. items.title: Morocco CyberSecurity Week : Orange Maroc renforce son engagement pour la cyber-résilience et un numérique de confiance
items.description: Orange Maroc participe à la Morocco CyberSecurity Week 2026, qui se tient du 12 au 14 octobre à Rabat, en qualité de Sponsor Silver – Cloud & Security Partner. Placé sous le thème « La cybersécurité au service de la transformation et du développement numérique », cet événement constitue un rendez-vous majeur pour les acteurs engagés dans la construction d'un écosystème numérique sûr et résilient. À travers cette participation, Orange Maroc réaffirme son engagement en faveur d'une transformation numérique de confiance, convaincu que la prévention, l'anticipation des risques et le renforcement de la cyber-résilience sont des conditions essentielles au développement durable de l'économie numérique marocaine. Trois initiatives stratégiques pour renforcer l'offre de cybersécurité et de cyber-résilience d'Orange Maroc À l'occasion de cette édition, Orange Maroc met en avant trois initiatives stratégiques avec Fortinet, NETSCOUT et Ivanti, illustrant sa volonté de renforcer ses expertises et d'enrichir son offre de cybersécurité. Ces collaborations répondent à des enjeux complémentaires : la sécurisation des environnements industriels et critiques, la cyber-résilience des réseaux et la protection proactive des terminaux. Avec Fortinet, Orange Maroc s’appuie sur l’obtention de la spécialisation Operational Technology (OT) pour renforcer son expertise dans la sécurisation des environnements industriels et des infrastructures critiques, ainsi que sa capacité à répondre aux enjeux de convergence IT/OT et de protection des équipements connectés. Le partenariat avec NETSCOUT évolue quant à lui au-delà de la protection contre les attaques DDoS, vers une approche élargie de la cyber-résilience, combinant visibilité avancée sur les réseaux, détection intelligente des menaces et protection adaptative. Enfin, la collaboration avec Ivanti vient enrichir l’offre de cybersécurité d’Orange Maroc à travers une approche proactive et automatisée de la sécurisation des terminaux (endpoints), associant visibilité en temps réel, priorisation des risques et remédiation prédictive. « À l'heure où l'IA accélère la transformation numérique et fait évoluer les menaces, la cybersécurité est devenue un pilier essentiel de toute transformation réussie. Notre ambition est d'accompagner les entreprises et les administrations marocaines dans la sécurisation de leurs activités, en combinant une connaissance approfondie de leurs enjeux avec un écosystème technologique et partenarial global. À travers notre engagement, nous contribuons à construire un environnement numérique plus sûr, plus résilient et propice au développement économique » , souligne Nouhade Mechkour, ICT Director d'Orange Maroc. Orange Maroc contribue également aux réflexions stratégiques du Forum à travers les interventions de ses experts. Nouhade Mechkour, ICT Director, prend part au panel consacré aux enjeux d'une transformation Cloud fiable et sécurisée, tandis qu'El Mehdi Benaabd, Head of ICT Solution and Product Engineering, intervient sur le rôle du marché de la cybersécurité comme moteur de croissance et d'innovation. À travers cette participation et le renforcement de son écosystème de partenaires technologiques, Orange Maroc réaffirme son ambition d'accompagner durablement la transformation numérique du Royaume, en faisant de la cybersécurité un levier de confiance, de résilience et de compétitivité pour l'ensemble de l'écosystème. The post Morocco CyberSecurity Week : Orange Maroc renforce son engagement pour la cyber-résilience et un numérique de confiance appeared first on Hespress Français - Actualités du Maroc .

items.title: Omani FM arrives in Pakistan for Joint Ministerial Commission session
items.description: Omani Foreign Minister Sayyid Badr Albusaidi arrived in Pakistan on a two-day visit on Tuesday, during which he would head his country’s delegation at the eighth Pakistan-Oman Joint Ministerial Commission (JMC) session. According to the Foreign Office (FO), he was received upon his arrival by the Economic Affairs Division secretary and the foreign ministry’s additional secretary (Middle East). He would also hold a bilateral meeting with Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar during his stay in Pakistan, the FO statement said. In an earlier statement, the FO had said the JMC session would “serve as an important platform to review the entire spectrum of Pakistan-Oman bilateral relations and to further strengthen cooperation in diverse fields”. The visit “reflects the longstanding fraternal relations between Pakistan and Oman and is expected to further deepen mutually beneficial cooperation across multiple sectors”, it had added. On Saturday, DPM Dar chaired an inter-ministerial meeting in Islamabad to review the preparations for the upcoming JMC session, according to state-run Radio Pakistan. The meeting reviewed the agenda, bilateral agreements and arrangements for the co-chairing of the JMC session, it said. According to Radio Pakistan , the session will focus on “deepening cooperation in trade, investment, industry, agriculture, finance, oil and gas, labour, consular affairs, security, defence, climate change, civil aviation, education, media, and culture”. Dar highlighted the importance of the commission in strengthening bilateral relations. He directed stakeholders to ensure thorough preparations and effective follow-up to “secure tangible outcomes”, the report added.

items.title: Décentralisation : Le conseil municipal de Bas-Mono 1 ouvre sa 4eme session ordinaire
items.description: Afagnan, 13 oct. (ATOP) – Les travaux de la 4 eme session ordinaire de l’année du conseil municipal de Bas-mono 1 ont été ouverts, le lundi 12 octobre à Afagnagan. Cette session sera essentiellement consacrée à l’examen et à l’adoption du budget primitif exercice 2027 de la commune. Pendant dix jours, les conseillers municipaux vont plancher sur les grandes orientations financières de la commune pour l’année prochaine avec un focus sur la mobilisation des ressources et la priorité des investissements. L’assistance Outre le budget, les travaux vont porter également sur le compte rendu des commissions permanentes, l’analyse de la situation des recettes et des dépenses, le bilan des activités de l’état civil, des mandatements et des services techniques notamment la topographie et l’état d’avancement des infrastructures. Il est aussi prévu la délibération sur la création du service de la voirie et d’autres questions d’intérêt communal. Le préfet de Bas-Mono, Sogbo Kokou Amétépé a relevé l’importance du débat budgétaire dans la préparation du budget communal. Selon lui, il permet aux élus locaux d’examiner les perspectives financières de la commune, d’identifier les priorités d’intervention et d’apprécier les moyens sensibles à mobiliser pour répondre aux besoins de la population. « Il s’agit avant tout d’un moment de réflexion stratégique qui doit permettre à la commune de faire des choix réalistes, responsables et cohérant avec ses capacités financières ainsi qu’avec les attentes légitimes des citoyens », a précisé M. Sogbo. Le préfet a invité les conseillers à privilégier les investissements susceptibles d’apporter des réponses concrètes aux préoccupations quotidiennes des populations. Le 1 er adjoint au maire, Romain Dansou a réaffirmé la volonté, la disponibilité et l’engagement du conseil à œuvrer pour le développement local et le bien-être des citoyens. M. Dansou a invité les différents acteurs à participer activement aux débats en vue de contribuer à l’amélioration des conditions de vie des populations. ATOP/DK/BA

items.title: Saudi Arabia: Death Penalty for Facebook Comment
items.description: Click to expand Image Anojan Sivarasa. © Private (Beirut) – A Saudi court has sentenced a Sri Lankan migrant worker to death over a Facebook comment that was deemed blasphemous, Human Rights Watch said today. Saudi authorities should reverse the judgment and release him immediately. The Saudi Court of Appeal in the Eastern Region handed down the death sentence to Anojan Sivarasa, 24, on September 17, 2026, after two court sessions. An initial ruling had sentenced him to five years in prison. “Sentencing a migrant worker to death over a Facebook comment that he has publicly apologized for is an outrageous overreaction from Saudi authorities amid a surge in executions,” said Joey Shea, senior Saudi Arabia researcher at Human Rights Watch. “No one should face execution for a comment on religion.” On June 28, Sivarasa replied to a video circulating on Facebook with a comment in Tamil deemed offensive to the Prophet Muhammad by some viewers. The comment quickly gained attention, and a screenshot was apparently sent to Saudi authorities and Sivarasa’s employer, a family member of Sivarasa’s told Human Rights Watch. Sivarasa deleted the comment and uploaded an apology video to his Facebook account. Sivarasa’s employer held him in its office for at least 24 hours and then took him to the Dammam police station, where he was arrested on July 1, the family member said. Sivarasa was working in construction and had arrived in Saudi Arabia just 10 months earlier. He is the sole breadwinner for his family in Sri Lanka, the family member said. The Al-Ahsa Public Prosecution charged Sivarasa with “verbally insulting and offending our Prophet Muhammad” and “producing and disseminating, through the information network, material prejudicial to religious values and public morals, by publishing a comment on a social media program containing words contrary to religious values and public morals,” according to court documents obtained by Human Rights Watch. On July 27, the Criminal Court of Al-Ahsa issued a judgment convicting Sivarasa under article 6 of the Anti-Cyber Crime Law and sentenced him to five years in prison and a fine of 3 million Saudi riyals (about US$800,000), according to court documents. The court also ordered confiscation of his electronic device and closure of his Facebook account. The Al-Ahsa Public Prosecution filed an appeal of the initial judgment. Sivarasa’s lawyer also appealed the initial judgment and sentence. On September 17, Sivarasa informed his family that he had been sentenced to death, the family member said. Court documents reviewed by Human Rights Watch show that Court of Appeal in the Eastern Region found Sivarasa guilty of verbally insulting the Prophet Muhammad on a social media post and sentenced him to death. “We never expected this situation,” the family member said. “This is a funeral house. The family is shocked and they still are recovering from that state of shock.” On October 5, a prisoner attacked Sivarasa in detention with a small weapon, injuring his head and face. the family member said. He received medical attention and has been moved to a different cell. Saudi Arabia has executed more than 2,000 people over the last decade, in many cases violating Saudi and international law. Authorities executed at least 356 people in 2025, setting a new record in the country for the highest number of executions in one year since monitoring began. International human rights law, including the Arab Charter on Human Rights ratified by Saudi Arabia, obliges countries that use the death penalty to only do so for the “most serious crimes” and in exceptional circumstances. Human Rights Watch opposes the death penalty in all circumstances because of its inherent cruelty. “Saudi Arabia should immediately quash this sentence and release Sivarasa,” Shea said. “Saudi authorities should end their use of abusive laws to hand out extraordinary sentences for speech-related offenses, especially against migrant workers who are already in a vulnerable position with limited protections.”
